articles.title: Fantasy Football: 4 players off the waiver wire worth stashing before the NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Chris Allen suggests you add these players proactively for fantasy football before the NFL Trade Deadline.
articles.body:
Every league has that one manager. You know the type. A starter goes down on Sunday afternoon, and before you can even refresh the waiver wire, you see the backup is already on their bench. They grabbed him two weeks ago. You check the transaction log, and they've been quietly stashing handcuffs and backups all season.

It's frustrating. But they're not lucky. They're just a step ahead.

The NFL trade deadline is next Tuesday, and that's our chance to be that manager. When a veteran gets shipped out, someone on the depth chart inherits his role. By Wednesday, that player is the top waiver claim, and everyone's throwing half their FAB at him. Or we can be proactive and make the move before the NFL decides for us. Here are the players worth stashing now who could benefit when their teammates get traded.

As of this writing, Keenan Allen sits at a 59% roster rate, so he's likely sitting on someone's bench in your league. But the Colts have a couple of pockets in their schedule that make the veteran WR a worthy target in negotiations independent of what happens on Tuesday. Three of his next four matchups will be against secondaries above the league average in PPG allowed to WRs. And he has a similar setup during the fantasy playoffs (at TEN, vs. CIN). More importantly, the volume has been there for Allen even with the current personnel in Indianapolis.

So, two things from this clip of Allen from last Sunday. First, look who's throwing to him. Anthony Richardson came in for the final few drives. He attempted only three passes. Two of those throws went toward Allen. Second, check the time. It's the fourth quarter, the team is down by double digits and the 34-year-old vet is still hoarding the opportunities. He had a 42.9% target share in the fourth quarter alone. But even before Week 8, Allen was siphoning looks away from the younger talent.

Targets per Route Run: 26.7%, 1st (of all Colts pass-catchers)

Of course, the immediate concern is tying yourself to Daniel Jones. Even before the Colts started making deals, Jones ranked 30th in CPOE amongst all starters. But he hasn't had any issues getting the ball to Allen. His 80% catchable target rate sits at ninth among all WRs (min. 175 routes). Even with Downs, Allen has WR3 appeal in PPR leagues. If the Colts come out the other side of the trade deadline minus one receiver, Allen becomes a low-end WR2.

So, I don't want to overreact to a few games of Ryan Flournoy playing well. That'd be a short-sighted, results-based take. Let's look at the bigger picture. Let's start in 2026.

EPA per Target: 0.33 (Lamb), 0.42 (Pickens), 0.34 (Flournoy)

First Downs per Target: 44.6%, 45.2%, 38.6%

Explosive Play Rate: 14.9%, 21.0%, 17.8%

At 44 targets through Week 8, Flournoy's workload is less than half of Lamb's, and he's 18 looks behind Pickens. But he's making a similar impact on the offense as the primary duo. Even though most of his routes only amount to him getting his cardio workout for the day, Flournoy has generated just nine fewer first downs than Pickens. He's averaging more YAC per reception than Lamb (4.8 yards to 3.5). However, before you say this guy came out of nowhere, let's go back to 2025.

Of the 93 WRs with 250 or more routes last year, Flournoy ranked 11th in first downs per route run. Across the 12 games where all three Dallas WRs were active, Dak Prescott had the highest passer rating when targeting Flournoy. He's also opened up running lanes for his teammates downfield as a blocker . Essentially, even if Dallas doesn't move on from Pickens, Flournoy's track record has shown he should be a larger part of the passing game. That's why the past few weeks, while irritating to gamers who roster Pickens, haven't been surprising.

Week 6: 12.9% (Plays w/ 2+ TEs), 4.3% (Plays w/ 6+ OL), 1.7% (Flournoy 2WR Snap Rate)

Over the past two weeks, Dallas' play-calling has shifted to being more run-focused (-11.4% and -2.8% PROE in Weeks 7 and 8). Typically, that'd pull Flournoy off the field in favor of the Cowboys' top two. Instead, he's played more and scored his second TD of the season in the process. Flournoy is already creeping into WR3 territory as TE production in Dallas wanes. If the WR room also thins out at the deadline, Flournoy could go from a WR3 to a weekly starter overnight.

Nick Singleton/Tyjae Spears, RBs, Titans

I already relived the rollercoaster my Bengals put me through on Sunday. But at least I got to do it from Joe Burrow's perspective . However, now I need to look at it from Tennessee's side. Because it's easy to say Tony Pollard has made himself a secondary option for teams in the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes. But he didn't do it on his own.

Just rewatching Pollard's TD run , he was four yards past the line of scrimmage before somebody in orange and black got a hand on him. But the line has been slowly giving him better lanes over the past month. His rushing success rate was as low as 35.7% in Week 5, but has steadily picked up to 50+% over the past two weeks. To go with the added efficiency, Pollard's rate of carries where defenders have met him at or behind the LoS has decreased (65% in Week 6 down to 42.9%). Coupled with the fact that the Titans' PROE falls to -9.7% when they're in scoring position, if Pollard had a new home by next Wednesday, Singleton, who has an RB1 athletic profile, would be able to excel in the right matchups. But they wouldn't have to do it as rushers alone.

While Tyjae Spears was healthy, Cam Ward was targeting his RBs on 19.6% of his dropbacks. Since then, it's been down to 12.0%. Despite averaging 21.7 attempts per game as the starter, Pollard has earned only 2.3 targets a week. Spears alone was up to an 11% target rate before getting injured. Assuming a change in the backfield rotation, his utility in PPR leagues should have FLEX appeal. But before you rush to the waiver wire, be sure to check out the Titans' schedule.

Tennessee will face Jacksonville in Weeks 10 and 12. They've allowed 68.3 rushing YPG all season. In other words, there won't be a line to acquire either RB via waivers. But if you check the wire afterward, you'll likely be able to stash either on your bench for free.

articles.title: Cody Rhodes reveals comedic WWE legend slammed him "hard" on a 4-wheeler after friendly fight turned ugly
articles.summary: Cody Rhodes has made a lot of friends backstage during his lengthy tenure in WWE.
articles.body: Cody Rhodes has made a lot of friends backstage during his lengthy tenure in WWE. Moreover, Rhodes revealed that he did not shy away from having a friendly banter with them on some occasions. articles.title: Mizzou AD posts letter advocating for change in SEC replay booth transparency
articles.summary: Mizzou AD Laird Veatch posted an open letter to fans Monday, saying Missouri "requested a formal review and response from the SEC regarding the officiating."
articles.body:
In an open letter to fans after several controversial rulings and officiating decisions in Mizzou's Nov. 7 loss to Texas in Columbia, Missouri athletic director Laird Veatch published an open letter to fans Monday advocating for change in the transparency of the Southeastern Conference 's replay review protocols.

The Mizzou AD also said the university "requested a formal review and response from the SEC" but, in line with conference expectations, will not publicize the contents of its conversations.

With a little more than two minutes remaining in the third quarter of Mizzou's 34-20 loss to Texas on Saturday, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was ruled to have fumbled on a third-and-10 play. The ball vaulted 14 yards past the line of scrimmage, and UT receiver Emmett Mosley V picked it up a while after it came to rest.

Because the play was ruled a fumble and not a forward pass, and because Texas picked it up, the Longhorns picked up a first down. Three plays later, Manning found wide receiver Jermaine Bishop Jr. on a third-down, 25-yard touchdown throw, sparking a game-ending 21-0 run to down the Tigers .

In his letter Monday to Mizzou fans, Veatch did not criticize any decisions made on the field or in the replay booth in Saturday's game.

The Tigers were on the wrong end of several reviewed decisions in addition to the fumble/forward pass ruling, including an overturned catch for wide receiver Cayden Lee in the third quarter, a catch from Donovan Olugbode along the sideline in the first quarter, and a potential intentional grounding ruling on Manning.

"To be clear, I don't believe in blaming or complaining about officiating," Veatch wrote in the letter. "Officials are human, and mistakes are part of the game. Coaches and players have to respond to those moments and find ways to overcome adversity. That is why I greatly respect and appreciate how Coach Drinkwitz handled his postgame response with the media and his team."

Instead, Mizzou, its athletic director and university president are asking for the SEC to consider making a change that has become common in other conferences: Providing live audio or video from its replay booth.

"After the game Saturday, we requested a formal review and response from the SEC regarding the officiating," Veatch wrote. "Consistent with SEC expectations, we will not make those conversations or responses public, other than that we have not received anything inconsistent with what the conference has already shared publicly.

"This experience has reinforced my belief that our lack of transparency in the replay booth, particularly when other conferences have taken steps to provide it, allows for an environment of speculation and mistrust. Together with President Choi, we will be strong advocates for that change within the SEC this offseason."

The SEC is the only Power conference that does not air live video or audio from its replay booth. The Big Ten and Big 12 began doing so this season, and the ACC began airing conversations about officiating decisions in 2025.

The SEC also does not allow for a designated pool reporter to ask questions to officials after controversial decisions, which is common in professional leagues.

When reached for comment by the Columbia Daily Tribune on Saturday after the game, the SEC provided the following statement on the fumble ruling.

"The ruling on the field was a fumble," an SEC official wrote in an e-mail to the Tribune. "In replay review it was determined there was not clear and obvious video evidence that he had firm control of the ball when the hand intentionally started forward in order to overturn the call."

Mizzou head coach Eli Drinkwitz and MU's players did not criticize the officials or any decisions in postgame media availability.

"If I say what I want to say, I'm going to get fined until I don't have any retirement, and I'm not going to do that because I'm not going to blame the officials," Drinkwitz said Saturday. "That'd be disrespectful to Coach Sark and his team."

Veatch complimented Drinkwitz for how he handled his postgame comments in the open letter to fans.

Missouri (6-3, 3-3 SEC) has three games left in the regular season, beginning with a trip to face newly No. 1-ranked Georgia on Saturday, Nov. 14 in Athens, Georgia.

The Tigers will then face Kentucky and Oklahoma in back-to-back weeks on Faurot Field to finish the regular season.

"It's OK to acknowledge that Saturday hurt," Veatch wrote. "In fact, our collective frustration and disappointment is evidence of how high our program expectations have elevated.

"Now let's turn our attention to Georgia and the opportunities ahead, including two huge home games against Kentucky and Oklahoma. Our coaches and players deserve our support, and I know this fan base will continue to show up with the passion and pride that make Saturdays in CoMo so special."

articles.title: Lakers Star Hits Injury Report as Another Star Returns to Action
articles.summary: Luka Doncic returns to action for the Lakers against the Hawks on Monday, but Austin Reaves hits the injury report as questionable and Quentin Grimes is out....
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are facing off with the Atlanta Hawks on Monday, and while they're getting one star guard back, the other may be out of action.

Luka Doncic missed Sunday's win over the Detroit Pistons with a back issue , but he'll be in action on Monday.

He might be without fellow guard Austin Reaves, though, as he's been listed as questionable on the team's injury report.

Why is Austin Reaves questionable for Monday's Lakers game?

Reaves is dealing with an illness, leading to his questionable status for Monday's game at the Hawks, as reported by Khobi Price of the California Post .

Reaves scored 43 on Sunday in Doncic's absence , and if he's out or limited on Monday, Doncic will likely have to pick up the slack, but that shouldn't be a problem for the Slovenian superstar.

He's averaging more than 40 points per game thus far this season, a truly incredible rate of scoring that could help him in his pursuit of his first MVP award.

It's possible that Doncic could score 50 points again, a level he's already reached twice this season on Oct. 25 against the Utah Jazz and on Nov. 6 against the Portland Trail Blazers.

This kind of scoring pace has only been seen once before in the last 40 years, the team noted on social media .

Through his first eight games, Doncic scored more than 300 points, and the only other player to ever do that was Michael Jordan in the 1988-89 season.

Even if Reaves is good to play with his questionable status, the Lakers will be down a guard.

Quentin Grimes is out with a right finger sprain, Price reports.

Grimes "banged his finger," coach JJ Redick said, and while X-rays showed no break, he'll need some time to recover.

With Grimes and possibly Reaves out as well, Monday is shaping up to be another Luka Doncic showcase.

Do you think Luka Doncic will score 50 points again against the Hawks?

articles.title: Antetokounmpo Says Heat Players Don’t Trust Each Other
articles.summary: Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo admits the team lacks trust after a blowout loss. Klay Thompson and Erik Spoelstra weigh in on the rocky start.
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo said the Miami Heat do not trust one another after a Monday loss to the Los Angeles Lakers. Miami surrendered 138 points in the defeat, falling to 2-5. The Heat have since improved to 4-6, but their early struggles have exposed serious problems on defense. The five-time All-Star made the comment during a rough start where Miami has been outscored by 53 points through 10 games. It is a stark admission from a player who joined the team in July after a blockbuster trade with the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Heat defense has been terrible despite having elite defenders on the roster. With six All-Defensive team selections to his credit, Center Bam Adebayo joins Antetokounmpo, a former Defensive Player of the Year. Yet the unit ranks 25th in the league. Klay Thompson, who played 13 minutes in the loss, told ESPN that the team needs to stay present. "It's important for all of us to stay present and not look too far ahead in the season," Thompson told ESPN. He added that the group must think week to week rather than focus on the postseason.

Heat coach Erik Spoelstra dismissed the idea that the team just needs more time to gel. "It can't just be on paper, and it can't just be reputation," Heat coach Erik Spoelstra said. He insisted that the culture must be backed by real actions. Spoelstra scoffed at the suggestion that the team simply needed time to fix these issues when asked. "I don't know, but we don't want to use that as an excuse," he said. "The league's not waiting."

Giannis and Klay Joined a Messy Situation

Klay Thompson gave up millions in contract value to join Miami this summer. He left the Dallas Mavericks to play alongside Antetokounmpo, whom he believes can still lead a great team. Thompson said he loves the organization's intensity and called the move a full-circle moment, since his dad played for Pat Riley. "That Heat culture is real," Thompson said. However, the 4-6 record indicates the team must improve significantly before achieving greatness or securing a playoff spot.

articles.title: Ryan Hopkins wins Big Ten freshman of the week honor after first career start
articles.summary: The Badgers quarterback had a strong start this weekend.
articles.body:
Wisconsin Badgers true freshman Ryan Hopkins shone in his first start, throwing for 241 yards and three touchdowns in the team's 31-10 win over the Rutgers Scarlet Knights.

That caught the eyes of Badgers fans, who were impressed by the freshman and began to ask why Hopkins hadn't been playing even earlier in the season. Well, the performance also caught the eye of the Big Ten, as Hopkins was named the Big Ten Freshman of the Week on Monday.

Here's what the Big Ten said in their statement on Monday about Hopkins's selection.

The true freshman quarterback made his first career start on Saturday in Wisconsin's 31-10 win vs. Rutgers

Recorded 241 yards and three scores on 18-of-24 passing, with his 241 passing yards tying for the third most for a Badger freshman in their debut since 1990

Hopkins' three passing touchdowns were the most by any freshman in the nation this week and his 200.6 passer rating led all FBS freshmen in week 10 action

Threw scores of 66, 21 and 11 yards, all to different Badger receivers, with eight different Badgers catching passes in the win

Last Wisconsin Freshman of the Week: Mason Posa (Nov. 10, 2025)

UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach won Offensive Player of the Week, Michigan State cornerback NihJay Burt won Defensive Player of the Week, and Michigan State kicker Liam Boyd won Special Teams Player of the Week.

Hopkins is the third Badger to win a weekly award this week. Colton Joseph was the Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week back in Week 5 during the team's win over Michigan State, and Sebastian Cheeks won Defensive Player of the Week two weeks ago.

He's set to start the rest of the way for the Badgers and will look to build on his performance this weekend against the Maryland Terrapins.

articles.title: ESPN grades Jaguars-Saints trade for Davon Godchaux
articles.summary: What grade did the Jacksonville Jaguars receive for their role in the Davon Godchaux trade with the New Orleans Saints?
articles.body:
What grade did the Jacksonville Jaguars receive for their role in the Davon Godchaux trade with the New Orleans Saints ?

According to Jordan Schultz , the Jaguars are sending a 2028 sixth-round pick to the Saints for Godchaux. The selection could become a 2027 sixth-round pick if the Jaguars acquire one via the comp pick formula or another trade.

Listed at 6-3, 330 pounds, Godchaux can help fill that run-stuffing, nose tackle role for the Jaguars, who are without DaVon Hamilton for the remainder of the season due to a quad injury.

Godchaux's impact won't always show up on the stat sheet, but his ability to take on blocks and occupy space can open up opportunities for others.

ESPN grades Jaguars-Saints Davon Godchaux trade

The Jaguars earned a B- for this trade from ESPN, while the Saints were given a B.

"In his 10th season in the league, Godchaux was playing just under 20 snaps per game for the Saints. His run stop win rate ranked in the 65th percentile among interior defenders this season, though he had struggled in the category the prior two years. Godchaux has a $1.3 million salary and is in the last year of his contract."

This was a trade that will give the Jaguars a needed boost, but also one that likely comes with a lower ceiling, hence ESPN's modest grade.

articles.title: Nate Oats announces Aden Holloway will return from suspension for Oakland game
articles.summary: The Alabama Crimson Tide are looking to start of the 2026-27 season at 3-0 as they face off against the visiting Oakland Golden Grizzlies on Monday evening,...
articles.body:
The Alabama Crimson Tide are looking to start of the 2026-27 season at 3-0 as they face off against the visiting Oakland Golden Grizzlies on Monday evening, and they'll have a boost in the lineup as well. Alabama head coach Nate Oats acknowledged that star guard Aden Holloway would return to the lineup following a suspension and would play starters minutes, as per Jon Rothstein of 247Sports.

Aden Holloway was serving a suspension by the university following drug related charges last season, while he had remained on the Alabama roster. The incident occurred during March of last season, right before the start of the NCAA Tournament, and Holloway missed the Crimson Tide's run to the Sweet 16 . He was suspended for five games, which included the three exhibition games that Alabama played.

Considered a five-star recruit coming out of high school, Holloway was in the midst of a breakout seasons with Alabama last year. He appeared in 28 games, including 27 starts, at a little over 28 minutes per game. As a junior, he averaged 16.8 points, 2.8 rebounds and 3.8 assists with splits of 48.1 percent shooting from the field, 43.8 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 86.4 percent shooting from the free-throw line.

Holloway is now in his senior year of college basketball eligibility after spending the past two seasons at Alabama. He initially began his college career at Auburn where he played his freshman year before entering the transfer portal.

The Crimson Tide are in the program's eighth season with Nate Oats at the helm as head coach. The team is currently ranked No. 20 in the men's college basketball AP top-20 poll.

articles.title: ESPN gives FSU basketball little room for error against Florida
articles.summary: ESPN’s Matchup Predictor gives Florida State just a 13.8% chance to beat No. 1 Florida at the Tucker Center.
articles.body:
Florida State basketball is off to a 2-0 start under Luke Loucks, but ESPN does not like the Seminoles' chances in their first major test of the season.

According to ESPN's Matchup Predictor , FSU has just a 13.8% chance to beat No. 1 Florida Gators on Tuesday night at the Donald L. Tucker Center. The Gators are given an 86.2% chance to win despite playing on the road.

The projection sets up a sharp contrast with Florida State's strong start. The Seminoles have yet to trail through two games, opening with a 113-69 win over the Florida A&M Rattlers before beating the Troy Trojans 91-68 in their home opener. FSU is averaging 102.0 points per game and has out-rebounded its first two opponents 93-50.

Sebastian Rancik has led the offense at 21.5 points per game, while freshman center Marcis Ponder has recorded a double-double in each of his first two college games. Shon Abaev is also averaging six assists per game with just one turnover through the opening week.

Florida represents a much different challenge.

The Gators entered the season ranked No. 1 in both the AP and US LBM Coaches polls and are also 2-0. Florida opened with a 77-67 win over No. 14 Miami before cruising past Jacksonville 88-57. The Gators have shot 43.1% from 3-point range and are averaging 48 rebounds per game.

Florida has also won the last five meetings in the rivalry, including a 78-76 victory over FSU last season. The Gators lead the all-time series 49-28.

Still, Tuesday offers Loucks and the Seminoles an early opportunity to change the perception around this team. FSU has looked dominant through two games, and now it gets a chance to test that start against the top-ranked team in the country.

Florida State and Florida tip off at 6 p.m. ET Tuesday at the Tucker Center, with the game airing on ESPN2.

articles.title: Spurs rule out Devin Vassell for Monday night's game at Phoenix
articles.summary: It will be the first game this season without the seventh-year forward, who is averaging 11.9 points, 3.8 rebounds and 3.1 assists.
articles.body:
PHOENIX - The red-hot Spurs will be without Devin Vassell when they face the Phoenix Suns on Monday night.

The Spurs, who have won eight games in a row, downgraded the starting forward from questionable to out because of left adductor tightness after shootaround at the Mortgage Matchup Center.

It's unclear when Vassell suffered the injury.

The seventh-year pro played 21 minutes in the Spurs' 125-103 pounding of Portland on Saturday night, finishing with 15 points on 4 of 8 from the field and 2 of 4 from 3-point range. He also had three assists, two rebounds and two steals.

Through 10 games this season, Vassell is averaging 30.0 minutes, 11.9 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.7 steals while shooting 35.6% from beyond the arc on 3.4 attempts and a team-high 96.2% from the free-throw line.

Forward Tobias Harris was also ruled out of Monday's game. The 16th-year player has yet to make his debut with the Spurs after suffering a calf injury in the first week of training camp.

The Spurs signed Harris to a two-year deal worth $31 million in the offseason.

articles.title: Jordon Hudson sues couple that allegedly leaked video of shirtless Bill Belichick on porch
articles.summary: Jordon Hudson is suing the owners of a Massachusetts rental home, alleging they shared porch-camera footage of a shirtless Bill Belichick and private informa...
articles.body:
Jordon Hudson is suing the owners of a Massachusetts rental property for their alleged connection to the release of a video that showed her then-boyfriend Bill Belichick shirtless and outside the home while Hudson was renting it in 2023.

In a civil lawsuit filed Friday in Suffolk County Superior Court, Hudson accuses the couple of invasion of privacy, breach of contract and unfair and deceptive conduct after the video, which was captured on a porch security camera, and "personal and private information about Ms. Hudson" were leaked online.

According to the complaint, that leak in November 2023 was the reason the public found out about the romantic relationship between the then-22-year-old former college cheerleader and the then-70-year-old coach of the New England Patriots , who now coaches the North Carolina Tar Heels .

"These outrageous violations of Ms. Hudson's privacy have, among other things, resulted in significant unwanted publicity and scrutiny of Ms. Hudson and her relationship with Mr. Belichick, which they had intended to remain private, and led to the ridicule and denigration of Ms. Hudson through numerous tabloid stories published by the media," the complaint states.

"This unwanted scrutiny and the ensuing media stories, which contain false information, has caused significant damage to Ms. Hudson, which would not have occurred had Defendants not leaked Ms. Hudson's personal and private information."

The Times was unsuccessful in attempts to reach the defendants for comment.

The complaint states that Hudson booked the rental house for four days through Airbnb in or around June 2023. During her stay, the filing states, Hudson received a text from one of the owners reminding her not to park in front of a neighbor's property. According to the complaint, the owner also texted Hudson "a link to a Ring video of a shirtless Mr. Belichick walking to and from the Property, which had been captured and saved without the knowledge or authorization of Mr. Belichick or Ms. Hudson (the 'Ring Video')."

Hudson then informed the defendant that privacy was important to them and asked if she could delete the video, the lawsuit states, to which she received the response: "We will delete it from ring, but as you know, unfortunately, videos are never totally deleted."

After the video was leaked and the relationship became public, the complaint states, the same defendant told Hudson, "I absolutely did not leak this video to twitter or anyone." But in May 2025, according to the filing, the owner told Hudson in a text that while they didn't release the video publicly, "we had sent it to a few people initially wondering is this him [Mr. Belichick], isn't it him and I don't know what happened from there."

The complaint also accuses the defendants of giving a second porch video of Belichick to journalist Pablo Torre, who aired it on his podcast that same month.

Hudson is requesting a jury trial and seeks unspecified damages and an order "enjoining Defendants from disclosing or disseminating any personal and/or private information related to Ms. Hudson to any third-party."

Multiple media outlets reported last month that Hudson and Belichick quietly ended their romantic relationship in late 2025 but remain close friends and business partners.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.body: Angel McCoughtry is pushing back against the backlash surrounding her recent comments about Caitlin Clark, and the former WNBA star is now raising the possibility of legal action. A podcast discussion about beauty and popularity in women's basketball has taken an unexpected turn, with McCoughtry accusing critics of twisting her words. The five-time WNBA All-Star has denied calling Clark ugly and suggested that the online reaction could have legal consequences. Her response has also brought renewed attention to the debate over appearance, popularity and recognition in women's basketball.Angel McCoughtry threatens legal action over Caitlin Clark remarksThe controversy began during Angel McCoughtry's appearance on the podcast Get to the Point last Thursday. When asked whether she considered Caitlin Clark pretty, the former Atlanta Dream forward laughed off the question and shifted the conversation towards Clark's Indiana Fever teammate Sophie Cunningham.Some fans interpreted her response as a slight against Clark and criticised the former WNBA star. However, McCoughtry has strongly rejected the suggestion that she insulted the Indiana Fever guard.Taking to Threads on Sunday, she questioned whether the claims made about her comments could amount to defamation."I never called Anyone ugly, those words never came out my mouth. I don't even think in that way. So when people lie and say you said something you didn't or paint a lying picture. Isn't that a defamation lawsuit?"Her response has added another layer to an already heated discussion involving one of the WNBA's biggest stars. McCoughtry's original argument focused on how physical appearance can influence public attention and commercial opportunities in women's basketball."In the NFL or the NBA, if you're good, you're good. In the WNBA, if you look pretty…you might not be the best player…I went to a conference, and everybody loved Indiana. They loved Caitlin Clark. I said, how many of you know Kelsey Mitchell? None of them raised their hand."She then used Cunningham as an example, pointing to the attention and commercial opportunities the Fever guard has received despite averaging single-digit points.Angel McCoughtry raises WNBA safety concerns after death threatsThe former Atlanta Dream star also revealed that speaking about Clark and the attention surrounding her has exposed her to disturbing online abuse."I've gotten death threats for covering Caitlin Clark. So, we need protection. I'm not in the league, so who's protecting me when I have to cover issues about the league?"McCoughtry argued that the WNBA needs to take the safety of former players seriously, particularly those who continue to discuss league-related issues after retirement.She also raised concerns about financial protection for current players. According to McCoughtry, the league previously offered $100,000 to players who retired after completing at least 10 WNBA seasons.She questioned whether that amount was enough to cover the long-term costs of injuries and medical procedures. Podcast co-hosts Terrell Owens and Chris Spencer also expressed concern about the financial burden former athletes can face.The dispute has now moved beyond a discussion about Caitlin Clark's popularity. McCoughtry's comments have raised wider questions about online harassment, player protection and the pressures facing women in professional basketball.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Initiative launched to make UK world leader in women's sport
articles.summary: The FA, Team GB and England Netball are among major organisations to back the Equal Sport Project - a new initiative aimed at improving equality and making the UK world leaders for women and girls' sport.
articles.body:
The English Football Association, Team GB and England Netball are among major organisations to back the Equal Sport Project - a new initiative aimed at improving equality and making the UK world leaders for women and girls' sport.

Recent research by Sporting Insights found that fewer than 1% of women working in sport believe gender equality has been achieved across the industry, while more than half believe they are paid less than men for carrying out the same role.

Consequently, the Equal Sport Project has identified five areas where improved leadership, investment and action will have the greatest impact in bringing equality for women and men across sport. These are:

Equal access to sport for girls in school

Equal relevance, reach and revenue for women's sport

Governance structures redesigned for equality

Several organisations have already made pledges based on the above, including Aquatics GB and the FA prioritising female leadership programmes, while Sport England and UK Sport have committed to working with their funding partners to ensure their governance is designed by men and women, for men and women.

The Youth Sport Trust, meanwhile, has committed to support schools in recognising and challenging stereotypes as well as develop male allies to champion gender equality in PE, school sport and physical activity.

The project is also backed by the UK government, with sports minister Stephanie Peacock saying: "We have seen progress in women and girls' sport, but there is still a long way to go.

"Like the Equal Sport Project, this government is backing women's sport at every level, from hosting the 2027 Tour de France Femmes Grand Depart and bidding to host the 2035 Fifa Women's World Cup, to investing £400m in grassroots sport facilities, doubling priority access to football pitches for women and girls and chairing the Women's Sport Taskforce.

"We will work closely with the Equal Sport Project and encourage all organisations to get involved. Together we can make the UK a world leader in women and girls' sport."

articles.title: WWE Raw Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights After Crown Jewel 2026
articles.summary: On the heels of Crown Jewel, where Roman Reigns defeated Sami Zayn and Liv Morgan was upset by Chelsea Green, WWE Raw rolled into the Bon Secours Wellness Arena in historic Greenville, South Carolina, for the November 9 broadcast.
articles.body:
On the heels of Crown Jewel, where Roman Reigns defeated Sami Zayn and Liv Morgan was upset by Chelsea Green, WWE Raw rolled into the Bon Secours Wellness Arena in historic Greenville, South Carolina, for the November 9 broadcast.

What went down, how did it affect the build to the November 28 Survivor Series premium live event, and how did each match and segment grade out?

Find out in this recap of the latest episode.

An appearance from Intercontinental Champion "All Ego" Ethan Page

Bayley vs. Women's Tag Team Champion Michin

Iyo Sky and a Mystery Partner vs. Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez

Last Time in Action: Je'Von Evans and Penta defeated Bron Breakker and Austin Theory (Crown Jewel , November 7 )

New World Tag Team Champions Penta and Evans kicked off the night's show in a celebratory mood following their win over The Vision Saturday in Riyadh.

After a brief-yet-generic babyface promo, Bron Breakker appeared from out of nowhere and took both men down by himself. From there, The Badass called out Oba Femi, still fuming over The Ruler's interference in the tag title match at Crown Jewel.

Femi did not make him wait, hitting the ring and clotheslining the heel to the arena floor. The 2026 King of the Ring grabbed a mic, accepted Breakker's challenge, and we appeared to have the night's first match.

What a way to neuter the tag champions than by having Breakker take them out by himself. Kind of makes you wonder why he couldn't beat them Saturday with or without Theory.

Breakker vs. Femi on free TV? We will take it, but there's a big premium live event on November 28 that this once felt destined for.

Last Time in Action: Bron Breakker and Austin Theory lost to Je'Von Evans and Penta (Crown Jewel, November 7); Oba Femi defeated Bronson Reed (Money in the Bank, October 10)

With Theory, Logan Paul, and Maxxine Dupri watching from the floor, Breakker found himself on the defensive early and often in Monday's showdown with Femi.

A signature clothesline over the announcer's table and to the floor, though, turned the tide in Breakker's favor and put The Ruler on the defensive. Femi attempted a comeback, but he missed a corner charge, and Breakker regained control of the bout.

Femi recovered, tossed Breakker across the ring, then stunned him with a series of corner uppercuts, culminating in one that sent his opponent over the announcer's desk.

Later, Breakker delivered the spear, but Femi kicked out at two, not ready to let his momentous run in 2026 come to an end at the hands of the second-generation star.

Paul interfered, slid his trademark brass knuckles to Breakker, then provided the distraction that allowed the Badass to use them. Femi shook it off, though, and delivered a Fall From Grace. The Vision hit the ring, delivered a beatdown, and drew a disqualification.

Evans and Penta hit the ring to clear the heels and stand tall with the victor.

Femi defeated Breakker via disqualification

This was a fun, hot match to kick off the in-ring portion of the show, featuring two big powerhouses with above-average in-ring chemistry. This was not up to the level of their first match, but it was still fun and featured some good selling from Femi, who has not been asked to do much of that since joining the main roster.

Could we not have gotten to the outcome that we did without having Evans and Penta catch a beatdown and devalue them as tag champions in the opening segment?

Survivor Series Match Card Predictions 🔮

Last Time in Action: Ethan Page defeated Chad Gable (Raw, November 2)

"Ethan, you're just an a*****e," Chad Gable told the new Intercontinental Champion, one week after losing his title to "All Ego," moments after interrupting his braggadocious and egotistical celebratory promo.

Big Cass interrupted the proceedings and took credit for Page winning the IC title, then threw his name in the hunt for a championship opportunity.

AAA Cruiserweight Champion Rey Fenix arrived next, rightly pointed out that he beat Page the last time he was on Raw, and staked his claim for a title shot.

Raw general manager Adam Pearce eventually appeared and made a No. 1 Contender's Match featuring Fenix, Cass, and Gable.

The grade here can be completely attributed to Page's work on the mic.

"Big Cass...you are tall," was a hilarious line about the big man's attributes.

Fenix making his case for a title opportunity by recalling his victory over Page made so much sense, it almost did not belong here.

Last Time in Action: Rey Fenix, Chad Gable, and Dragon Lee defeated The Vanity Project (NXT, November 4); Big Cass and Ethan Page defeated Gable and Lee (Raw, October 26)

Fenix will have the opportunity to add the Intercontinental Championship to his AAA Cruiserweight Championship after defeating Gable and Cass in an action-packed Triple Threat Match.

Cass launched Gable over the announcer's table at one point, but the former Olympic athlete fought back. He shook off a bloodied mouth and looked to have a win in hand at one point, but the stinger in his neck, shoulder, and arm that plagued him last week reared its ugly head.

Fenix eventually launched himself off the top rope with a frog splash and pinned the less-than-healthy former IC champion to score the win and earn a title shot.

His celebration was short-lived, though, as 946 hit the ring and beat down all three men.

Sitting in a steel chair, with the result of chaos surrounding him, Royce Keys told Roman Reigns the same fate awaits his family unless he acknowledges him.

The match was really strong, as should be expected any time Gable and Fenix are anywhere near a ring at this point. They have quickly become workhorses and in-ring standard-bearers.

Big Cass does not get nearly enough credit for being a hard-working big man who has proven he can perform at a high level against wrestlers of all sizes.

The 946 beatdown was excellent and Keys continues to find himself in his role of leader every single week. His screen presence here was off the charts and the facial expressions he flashed while addressing Reigns were phenomenal.

Last Time in Action: Cody Rhodes defeated Randy Orton (Crown Jewel, November 9)

Just 48 hours removed from his victory over The Viper in a Last Man Standing Match at Crown Jewel, The American Nightmare admitted to loving punting Orton in the head.

"Now that that nasty business is in the rear-view mirror," Rhodes said, before transitioning to the Team USA vs. Team Mexico match at Survivor Series. He called out the latter's captain, Rey Mysterio, for an in-ring discussion.

A civil conversation between the respected former world champions was interrupted by Dominik Mysterio.

Dirty Dom took exception to being left out of the conversation, then made his case for inclusion on both teams, despite taking a few shots at his father. "Get your punk-ass out of this ring," Rey told his son.

"We're gonna pass," Rhodes told the second-generation star.

CM Punk joined the fray, earning a thunderous ovation along the way, and threw his name in the mix for Team USA, with the idea of climbing back into title contention.

A frustrated Dirty Dom got himself into a physical interaction that ended with him and JD McDonagh suffering a 619 from Rey, followed by Cross Rhodes and Go To Sleep, respectively, to close out the segment.

There was some good comedy from all involved here, with all five guys appearing to have a blast.

Would it have been nice to have better explanation of the match and how the Superstars involved will be decided? Sure, but this is largely a match designed to get everyone outside of the Bloodline and 946 on the card and with that in mind, this worked.

The question now is whether Dom and McDonagh will make their presence felt in the build to the match and the contest itself in Houston.

Punk, Rhodes, and Mysterio's presence in the match certainly enhances it from a star power perspective if nothing else.

Last Time in Action: Bayley defeated Lyra Valkyria (Raw, October 26); Michin and B-Fab fought to a no-contest with Fatal Influence (SmackDown, November 6 )

Women's Tag Team Champion Michin weathered the storm that was Bayley's early onslaught, then caught her with a missile dropkick to seize control of the match entering the commercial break.

The heel continued her onslaught after the match, catching Bayley with a German suplex.

The Role Model absorbed everything thrown at her by her opponent, then fought back, ultimately delivering a flying elbow for the pinfall victory.

After the match, Jade Cargill and B-Fab hit the ring and jumped Bayley. Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, and Tatum Paxley looked to make the save but were attacked by Fatal Influence's Lainey Reid, Fallon Henley, and Women's United States Champion Jacy Jayne.

The heels beat down the babyfaces and stood tall to close out the segment.

Bayley and Michin had a really strong little match here, proving that the latter can hang with a future Hall of Famer when given the chance to and not having her matches interrupted with incessant interference and chicanery.

The post-match beatdown felt like a given after the babyfaces got the best of the heels on SmackDown.

Rhea Ripley makes perfect sense as the woman to round out the Babyface side and fight off the heels, but she still recovering from a knee injury so who knows what her availability is.

Iyo Sky and Becky Lynch vs. Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez

Last Time in Action: Iyo Sky, Chelsea Green, and Tiffany Stratton lost to Roxanne Perez, Raquel Rodriguez, and Liv Morgan (Raw, November 2); Becky Lynch defeated Morgan via disqualification (Raw, October 26)

The Genius of the Sky introduced The Man as her mystery partner for Monday's match, the latest in the duo's rivalry with the women of the Judgment Day in recent months.

The heels beat down and isolated Sky throughout the commercial break. A tag to Lynch sparked a babyface comeback, but the heels downed Big Time Becks, allowing the Judgment Day to regain control.

Rodriguez benefited from a distraction from Morgan, blasted Lynch with a big boot, and delivered the Tejana Bomb to the former WrestleMania main eventer. Sky broke up the pin, though, and the match continued.

Lynch fended off Morgan and Perez on the floor and back inside the ring, Sky delivered the Over the Moonsault for the pinfall victory.

After the match, The Man formally issued a challenge to Morgan for a Women's World Championship Match, but received no response.

Lynch and Sky defeated Rodriguez and Perez

Rodriguez has quietly become a workhorse on the Raw brand, someone who regularly competes and more times than not, delivers. She has become a hidden gem in the company.

Can we get a good, long, perhaps premium live event match between Sky and Perez? That would be swell and probably steal the majority of the shows.

A finale in the Lynch-Morgan feud is much needed, so the prospects of one final title match are much anticipated.

Did Roman Reigns Acknowledge Royce Keys?

Last Time in Action: Roman Reigns defeated Sami Zayn (Crown Jewel, November 7); Royce Keys fought to a no contest with Solo Sikoa (Raw, November 2)

Keys joined Reigns in the ring, and it was only a matter of seconds before they revealed that neither came alone. While the 946 entered the arena, a video showed The Usos, Solo Sikoa, and returning Jacob Fatu outside the arena, burning down 946's truck.

Reigns rocked a distracted Keys with a Superman Punch, then unloaded on the rest of the group before the numbers game proved too great to overcome.

The Bloodline entered the arena and teed off on the 946 members. The Samoan Werewolf flattened Carmelo Hayes, then laid him out on the commentary table. He added a big splash from the top rope, driving the heel through it.

As the heels retreated, Reigns grabbed a mic and officially laid down the challenge: War Games.

If ever there was a time to do a heel beatdown that got interrupted by the returning Superstar, this was it. It would have been a huge moment for Fatu and given him a chance to re-establish his main event momentum.

With that said, this was still extremely well done, with the Bloodline finally getting over on their rivals and laying down the gauntlet for War Games.

This is the first match of its kind to actually feel deserving of the War Games gimmick in several years.

There was not one glaring MVP but Keys was excellent tonight. He did everything he had to, exhibited the character work that is essential to his growth and evolution, and looked the part of a main event star on the flagship show.

Solid in-ring action, strong build to Survivor Series, and some great stuff in the show-closing segment helped establish a "B" grade for this one, though it could have been even better without that questionable booking of the tag champions at the top of the broadcast.

articles.title: Washington Commanders report card: How we graded the Week 9 loss
articles.summary: Here's how we graded each unit in the Washington Commanders' Week 9 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders can't seem to figure things out this season. They started out pretty well against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, but then fell apart in the second half and couldn't get anything going. It was a long day for the defense, which spent entirely too much time on the field, and it was a frustrating day for the offense, which couldn't move the ball down the field.

We all know there are definite areas of opportunity for the Commanders, but there are things they're doing well as a team. While it may feel like there's no hope for this season, the truth is, we're only halfway through it and if they can turn things around, maybe they can at least end the season on a strong note.

Let's take one last look at this win and see how we graded the Commanders in our Week 9 report cards.

Someone on this offense has to step up and take a strong leadership stance. Jayden Daniels missed some easy, open throws that could have changed the outcome of the game, including one on the second-to-last drive of the game. We'll dig into his play in another section, but his performance weighs heavily on how the offense is graded as a whole.

The ground game continues to be nonexistent, with just 60 yards on the ground on Sunday. Rachaad White at least averaged four yards per carry, but with only seven carries, that didn't get them far. Austin Ekeler averaged just two yards per carry. That is never going to be good enough in this league, regardless of who you play. Washington has to find a way to get yards on the ground so the rest of the playbook can open up.

As far as pass-catchers go, Van Jefferson was the best wide receiver on Sunday, and that's a tad concerning. No one was winning deep, and no one was making Daniels' job any easier. That last part includes the offensive line because Daniels' protection wasn't good on Sunday. The entire offense needs to get their heads back in the game and figure out how to work with the personnel it has on hand.

Some people might be surprised by this grade given the Commanders' loss, but we want to point back to the offensive struggles again and understand that the defense was gassed by the fourth quarter. And, honestly, if Puka Nacua didn't have 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown, the defense might even get an A here.

If you look closely at the game, the defense actually played well enough to win this game. They needed to put more pressure on Matt Stafford, but they did enough to disrupt his rhythm and make him falter more than once. Even with Nacua's 14 catches, he didn't crush the defense with deep, explosive plays. The catches were short, contested catches that were well-defended, including Trey Amos' coverage on Nacua's touchdown.

Despite the loss, the defense played well, and it has been a bright spot for this team over the last few weeks.

The Rams did a great job with their kickoffs, limiting Luke McCaffrey's ability to return them. Only two kicks were returned: one for 22 yards and one for 20 yards.

For the Commanders, Drew Stevens was perfect on field goals and extra points again. His consistency is improving, and that's what Washington needs from him. His kickoffs need some work, but the coverage on kickoffs was solid. Only one kick was returned for 29 yards.

Tress Way is always good, and on Sunday he was his usual phenomenal self. He averaged 47 yards per kick with great hang time. Three of his punts landed inside the 20, and the Rams had no punt return yardage.

The offense struggled so much that it was a very rough day for offensive coordinator David Blough. The sad part is that most of it was self-inflicted, including on the Commanders' last drive. That final play call and execution were strange. Plus, Blough didn't make any adjustments to Myles Garrett, which is not only mind-blowing, but inexcusable. Your job as a coach is to make adjustments to give your players the best possible shot at winning. If you're not making adjustments, nothing is going to change.

Daronte Jones' defense was good, for the most part. He needed to find a way to force Nacua to earn more of his catches. There was way too much cushion at the line of scrimmage on many of the snaps, and that just opens up space for Nacua to wiggle away and make an easy grab. He's not a guy you can let run freely; someone has to stick to him and make him work for his yards.

Daniels put up decent numbers with a lot of dink-and-dunk plays. Most of that was by design because the Rams put so much pressure on Daniels, and the Commanders' best deep-ball threats are all injured (Terry McLaurin, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown). In the first half, Daniels missed an easy completion to Rachaad White that would have kept the drive going, but instead resulted in punting the ball away. He missed another easy pass to Van Jefferson with two minutes left in the fourth quarter, which turned the ball over on downs. That pass would have easily put the Commanders in the red zone, or even set them up for a touchdown to tie the game.

Daniels has to get a handle on his play just as much as the coaching staff has to get a handle on the play calling. There is a disconnect somewhere with this team, and until they find it and fix it, they will continue to struggle.

articles.title: Nate Oats 'happy' with Aden Holloway after Alabama basketball season debut, but wants more
articles.summary: Alabama basketball got back the most experienced piece of its backcourt. What Nate Oats thought of Aden Holloway's return after a 5-game suspension.
articles.body:
Check out our Alabama basketball vs Oakland photo gallery, best images

Alabama basketball had plenty of offensive firepower without its most experienced guard in the rotation. Against Oakland, one of the nation's most skilled perimeter shooters returned to action, and the Crimson Tide got a glimpse of just how much more dangerous it could become with Aden Holloway in the mix.

It had been almost eight months since Holloway suited up for Alabama (3-0), but after a slow start on Monday, Nov. 9, the senior showed fans in Coleman Coliseum that he's still got it − especially from deep.

Here are three takeaways from Holloway's performance, his impact on the Crimson Tide 's offense and what else coach Nate Oats wants out of him after Game 1.

How Aden Holloway performed in Alabama basketball return

Holloway's debut against Oakland (0-4) came after a five-game suspension stemming from a marijuana arrest in March, which has since been dropped from his record after completing a second-chance program.

However, Monday wasn't his first time back out on the court with the Crimson Tide since missing the team's most recent Sweet 16 run. Over the summer, Holloway continued to participate in workouts despite not officially being reinstated to the roster.

In his first appearance back with Alabama, Holloway went 4-for-8 from the floor, all of his shots coming from three-point range, and was the only player other than Kentucky transfer Brandon Garrison to play over 20 minutes. Holloway also registered two rebounds and two assists against one turnover while drawing three personal fouls.

Was there a difference in backcourt with Holloway in mix?

Having Holloway gave the Crimson Tide the chance to improve an offense that had generated plenty of shots through its first two games, but struggled to convert them consistently.

Alabama shot a combined 35.3% from the field and 29.4% from beyond the arc during the first halves against Sam Houston and Arkansas State. That marked a notable decline from the first three exhibition games, when the Crimson Tide converted 48.1% of its first-half field goal attempts and 37.3% of 3-pointers.

Holloway only had two of Alabama's 17 assists in the first half, but his impact spacing the floor translated to the box score.

Less than two minutes were left in the first period by the time Holloway made his first shot from deep, but it's hard to say he didn't contribute to perfect shooting performances from five other Alabama players − or the team's 66.7% shooting rate from the floor − at halftime.

Oakland may be the lesser of Alabama's first three regular season opponents, but the Holloway effect was measurable early.

In first halves against Sam Houston and Arkansas State, Alabama assisted on just 50% and 71.4% of shots, respectively. Against Oakland, the Crimson Tide assisted on 85% of its first-half baskets. Led by six from sophomore forward Amari Allen, Alabama finished with 30 assists, tying a program record.

"People are gonna see that stat and say, 'Wow, your defense must suck,' " Oakland coach Greg Kampe said, but he continued to argue that wasn't the case and felt his team guarded "unbelievable" Alabama adequately.

Kampe also noted that during preparation, he was "unaware" Holloway was playing until he was informed by his staff.

"I didn't know 2 existed until my staff told me, 'Hey, this kid's gonna play tonight,'" Kampe said.

What else Nate Oats wants to see from veteran guard

Getting Holloway back out on the floor was one step. Establishing how he fits into the rotation for the remainder of the season is another.

Oats previously praised Holloway's personal growth during his suspension, pointing to maturity he demonstrated while away from competition that helped him become a leader the team needs. While he's happy with that, and Holloway's overall performance against Oakland, he still wants more rebounding from the Naismith Trophy Watch List member.

When asked for his review of Holloway's defensive performance, Oats grinned.

"I thought it was definitely better than he was for most of the games last year," he said. "I think there was a few games where he showed his capability, and particularly the one down at LSU. I thought this version of him is a lot more like we're going to see all year.

"I love his intensity. I like the fact, you know, he was staying in front of the ball. I liked his leadership tonight," Oats said, also shouting out Holloway for having one of the highest Blue Collar point totals.

Oats said Holloway will "have to be better" on Friday night against Seton Hall.

"But I thought he played pretty hard on that end for tonight," Oats said.

articles.title: India's chess GMs: 100 and counting – Why becoming a Grandmaster is now just a tiny step
articles.summary: When Viswanathan Anand became a Grandmaster in Coimbatore in 1988, attaining that step used to be a giant step towards professional chess.
articles.body: When Viswanathan Anand became a Grandmaster in Coimbatore in 1988, attaining that step used to be a giant step towards professional chess. Now, it’s a footnote. India completing a century of GMs on Sunday — with Anuj Shrivatri being the latest one with a win at the ASEAN Plus in the Philippines on Sunday — should be viewed accordingly.Though FIDE has lowered the regulations to attain a GM title, the players still have to find shortcuts and easier paths to add the accolade to their CV. These include pulling out, withdrawing and reentering from the pairings of the same tournament multiple times, withdrawing from one tournament in one city and travelling to the other city the next day. All this to protect an Elo drop in a bid to reach Elo 2500. Or playing soft tournaments in Europe.Becoming a GM is still a task, though, and further progress is even more difficult. Frequent and lucrative tournaments are available only for players above Elo 2650. If you don’t reach Elo 2550 by age 17, that final push is improbable. Though becoming a GM before age 18 is possible, it’s a full-time endeavour with escalating costs and entails huge compromises on academics and social life.Only 51 of India’s GMs have maintained a rating of more than Elo 2500. India’s current rating spread of GMs is from Elo 2763 (Pragg) to Elo 2222 (Saptarshi Roy Choudhary). There are nine GMs in India aged 15-25 who are below the minimum GM rating of Elo 2500, with the lowest being Prithu Gupta at 2398, the India No. 142 and not among 3,000 best players in the world.When Anand became a GM there were less than 200 active GMs rated above Elo 2500, now there are about 550. And if we count GMs who have slipped below Elo 2500, there are about 750 more GMs the world over. The situation is dramatically better for women who manage to attain GM title after hardships including social and emotional challenges.“Generally, the players have to pay huge amounts as coaching fees and most of the GMs today are unemployed or unsponsored. There are many others who spend these types of funds but never ever cross the rating of Elo 1900. Private sponsors and funding for coaching is very small in number compared to the aspirants trying to get titles in India,” Pravin Thipsay, former seven-time National champion and coach, told TOI.“It’s sad that unlike the Soviet Chess Federation or the Russian Chess Federation or Chinese Chess Federation, the AICF has not attempted to create a system wherein the GMs and other merited players would be absorbed for training assignments or for any other form of services by which a player could get reasonable financial benefits,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Finally, Purdue basketball finds its offense late to run off Illinois State
articles.summary: Jack Benter and Antione West Jr. earned starts and were the key players during Purdue's late run to beat Illinois State at Mackey Arena.
articles.body:
WEST LAFAYETTE — At last, Purdue basketball fans can breathe a sigh of relief.

It took huge late run to blow the game open, but the Boilermakers left Mackey Arena with their first victory.

A lineup change that included Jack Benter and Antione West Jr. among the starters helped pilot Purdue 's 76-59 win over Illinois State on Monday, Nov. 9.

Purdue (1-2) led 50-48 midway through the second half before landing the knockout blow it needed after losses to Gonzaga and Valparaiso to open the season while also snapping out of its 3-point shooting funk.

After combining to shoot just 20.4% from 3 in the first two games, the Boilers made 8 of 19 against the Redbirds (1-2).

Purdue basketball turning point vs. Illinois State

Despite a hot shooting first half, Purdue couldn't separate itself from the Redbirds.

Illinois State had a chance to cut the lead to two, but Louie Semona II's 3-pointer was off and Enzo Shahrvin pulled down the rebound. Purdue called timeout to set up a final play. Antione West Jr. ended up making a stepback 3-pointer from the right wing to give the Boilermakers a 36-28 halftime lead.

That shot was Purdue's saving grace for a long time, but it was just enough to keep Illinois State from ever pulling even or going ahead. Eventually, Purdue found its footing and blew the game open with a 24-2 run relying on a lineup of Antione West Jr., Luke Ertel, CJ Cox, Jack Benter and Daniel Jacobsen.

Jack Benter received his first two career starts out of necessity when Trey Kaufman-Renn was sidelined to open last season. On Monday, the junior was in the starting rotation for the first time in a year. He showed what he's capable of from the get go, sinking a 3-pointer for the game's first points, then drawing a charge on the defensive end.

It set the stage for a productive night across the board for Benter, who finished with 14 points, 5 rebounds, 3 assists and a steal.

3 Purdue basketball standouts vs. Illinois State

Daniel Jacobsen: Three games in a row is a trend. The 7-foot-4 center is Purdue's best offensive piece. It was another stellar night for the Boilermaker big man, contributing his third straight game with at least 20 points, hitting that number on the nose. Jacobsen also had 7 rebounds and 3 assists.

Antione West Jr.: In his first career start after sitting out last season, West had a coming out party. West scored 17 points on 7 of 11 shooting and added 2 rebounds, 2 assists and a steal.

CJ Cox: The junior guard made three early midrange jumpers. He didn't fill up the stat sheet, but he didn't hurt the Boilermakers either. Cox had 10 points, 3 assists and, in typical Cox fashion, no turnovers.

articles.title: Bears’ Ben Johnson Comments on Potential Trades Before the Deadline
articles.summary: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson shared his thoughts on potential trades before the deadline on November 10th. The post Bears’ Ben Johnson Comments on Po...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears could still have some decisions to make before the NFL trade deadline, and head coach Ben Johnson recently addressed whether the organization could pursue additional reinforcements.

With the Bears entering their bye week and the November 10th deadline approaching, general manager Ryan Poles has limited time to determine whether the roster needs another addition for the second half of the season.

Chicago has already made a significant move by acquiring defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans, sending two firsts and a fourth-round pick, but Johnson's latest comments suggest the organization isn't necessarily finished exploring the trade market.

Bears News: Ben Johnson Addresses Potential Moves Before the Trade Deadline

During a media session on November 9th, Ben Johnson was asked about the unusual situation of having a bye week while simultaneously having to evaluate potential roster improvements before the trade deadline.

A reporter specifically asked how the next 22 and a half hours would look for the Bears as they determine whether their remaining weaknesses can be addressed internally or whether additional reinforcements are necessary.

Johnson pointed toward Ryan Poles and the coaching staff's ongoing discussions about potential improvements.

"I think Ryan's doing a phenomenal job every day he's going through and seeing how we can improve this roster. What we need the most of. The coordinators are certainly talking every day right now just where their concerns lie within the roster. And so we'll see."

Johnson didn't rule out the possibility of Chicago making another move before the deadline, suggesting that Poles and the coaching staff are still evaluating their options.

"We'll see if there's another move or two to be made or if we stand put."

Knowing Poles, he won't be afraid to make another trade. Even if the Bears already gave up significant draft capital for Jeffery Simmons.

Bears Could Make Another Move Despite Johnson's Confidence

Although Johnson left the door open for another trade, he also made it clear that he believes Chicago already has enough talent in the locker room to remain competitive.

"I feel really confident about the guys that we have in this locker room right now that I think they've proven at this point that we can find a way to win each and every week with this group," Johnson said.

I love the confidence, but the Bears could use some help at certain positions, including cornerback.

There's been some buzz surrounding Chicago potentially trading for Philadelphia Eagles CB Riq Woolen, especially now that Eagles GM Howie Roseman sent Jordan Davis away to the Jacksonville Jaguars .

Woolen recently commented on the trade rumors, saying, "If it's up to Howie the GM and my agent then I'm gonna leave it to them but me, knowing me as a person, I've worked hard with these guys and I'd love to be here and stay here with them."

With the November 10th deadline approaching, the Bears' next decision could provide another indication of how aggressively the organization plans to compete in 2026.

articles.title: Valtteri Bottas Out Before the Start as Cadillac Hit New Low in Brazil
articles.summary: The American team continues its cavalry charge in the 2026 F1: Bottas could not start due to a nut issue, Pérez finished eighteenth after another slow stop,...
articles.body:
Cadillac still cannot find the light in its debut season in Formula 1. The American team, which has not yet scored a single point in 2026, entered a new chapter of its particular Calvary at the Brazilian Grand Prix.

Valtteri Bottas couldn't even take the start because of a nut issue in his car, while Sergio Pérez, the team's only on-track representative, finished eighteenth after a slow new pit stop. A weekend to forget, leaving Cadillac as the only team on the grid that has not managed to score.

Bottas's problem was the first blow of Sunday: the Finn, who had already crashed in Mexico due to a suspension failure, saw his race end before it began.

A wheel-nut issue kept his car in the garage, and the team confirmed he could not take the start. Another setback for a 37-year-old driver who continues to wait for an opportunity to prove his talent in a competitive car.

Pérez, for his part, could run at Interlagos, but his race was marked by another slow pit stop. The Mexican, who had shown a decent pace in the first laps, lost valuable seconds when his team took time to change his tires, a problem that had already been repeated in Mexico.

Despite this, the man from Guadalajara managed to cross the finish line in eighteenth place, ahead of Carlos Sainz and Rafael Camara, the Brazilian debutant in the Haas seat.

Camaro, debuting in his home race after replacing Esteban Ocon, did not have the dream day; the Brazilian, who showed flashes of talent in the wet qualifying, finished last among drivers who have disputed at least one race this season. His debut in Formula 1, although historic, was marked by his Haas's lack of pace and the challenges of a circuit as demanding as Interlagos.

Cadillac's situation is worrying. The American team that entered Formula 1 with high ambitions and General Motors' backing has not scored a single point in its first season.

Reliability problems, slow pit stops, and the MAC26's lack of performance have weighed down a team that, for now, has known only the back of the grid. The arrival of Mike Elliott as the new technical director and the construction of the engine factory in Charlotte are the hopes of a project that aspires to change course in 2027.

Meanwhile, the 2026 season advances, and Cadillac still hasn't found its place; with only three races left, the chances to score points have shrunk, but the team hasn't lost hope. Pérez, Bottas, and the young talents who have joined the American car will keep fighting for every tenth; Formula 1 does not forgive, and Cadillac is learning that the hard way.

The future will tell whether this year's work bears fruit, but for now, the reality is stubborn: Cadillac remains the red lantern of the grid.

articles.title: In Photos: Imangazaliev, Black Panther, And PTT Showcase Firepower At The Inner Circle Open Workout
articles.summary: The three Venum Training Camp and Team Mehdi Zatout stars display their elite striking in Pattaya, Thailand.
articles.body:
Reigning ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Champion Asadula "The Dagestan Ninja" Imangazaliev and Thai warriors Black Panther and PTT Apichart Farm showed their skills at an open workout last week at Venum Training Camp in Pattaya, Thailand.

The three stars of Venum Training Camp and Team Mehdi Zatout also spoke to media ahead of their upcoming fights at The Inner Circle 38 on Friday, November 13, and The Inner Circle 39 on Friday, November 20. Both events take place inside the fabled walls of Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, streaming exclusively for members via live.onefc.com .

The 23-year-old Russian headlines The Inner Circle 39, where he defends his crown for the first time against Aslamjon "El Pantera" Ortikov in a rematch. The clash also serves as the last quarterfinal bout of the 2026-2027 ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Grand Prix , with the winner advancing to the semifinals.

Imangazaliev is 13-0 and has built his reputation as an incredibly strong and unpredictable fighter who can finish a bout with any technique at his disposal. He became the first Russian athlete to capture Muay Thai gold in ONE Championship when he beat Ortikov in June, and now he wants to prove it was no fluke.

That first meeting at The Inner Circle 20 was the first time two undefeated stars from the weekly event series collided for a ONE World Title, and Imangazaliev edged it by split decision. This time, he is aiming for a more convincing win that leaves no room for debate, and one that sends him into the semifinal with his perfect record intact.

Before the main event, the penultimate quarterfinal of the tournament sees 26-year-old Black Panther take on undefeated Ubaid "Bad" Hussain at The Inner Circle 39.

The Thai striker is 82-17 overall and 6-1 in ONE. A technical fighter with a strong kicking game and powerful punches that come in bunches, he recovered from a losing start in the promotion and now rides a six-fight winning streak against world-class opposition. A win over Hussain would book his place in the semifinals.

That streak has included victories over the likes of Suriyanlek Por Yenying , Diego Paez and Johan Estupinan , and it has turned a promising newcomer into one of the most in-form strikers in the division. The Grand Prix gives him the biggest stage of his career and, with a semifinal spot on the line, he plans to keep his momentum rolling.

A week earlier, the 29-year-old PTT Apichart Farm meets Moroccan finisher Hamza Rachid in a bantamweight Muay Thai matchup at The Inner Circle 38.

The experienced Thai veteran owns a 114-25 career record and three wins in ONE, thanks to explosive power in his right hand and body kicks. After three straight victories, he suffered a loss in his most recent outing in June, and he is determined to get back on track against Rachid.

PTT has rebounded before. After a rough debut loss in the promotion, he turned things around in style and strung together impressive wins to establish himself as a name to watch in the division. Now he looks to show the same resilience against a dangerous finisher in Rachid and start a new run.

articles.title: Hornets’ Tidjane Salaun preaches consistency after huge 1st half vs. Cavs
articles.summary: The Charlotte Hornets have gotten off to a bit of a rough start to the 2026-27 season, winning just three of their first 10 games in the new campaign heading...
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets have gotten off to a bit of a rough start to the 2026-27 season, winning just three of their first 10 games in the new campaign heading into their Monday night clash against the Cleveland Cavaliers. Their offense has been downright bad, ranking dead last in the NBA with an offensive rating of just 99.7, and they seem to be missing LaMelo Ball, the driver of last season's fifth-best offense.

But on Monday, despite the absences of both Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel , the Hornets earned a statement win over the similarly struggling Cleveland Cavaliers, 124-112 in a game that wasn't as close as the final score line would suggest.

A big part of why Charlotte was able to dominate Cleveland was the strong play of Tidjane Salaun, who scored 14 points on a perfect 4-of-4 shooting display in the first half as they took a 16-point lead into the halftime interval. And during his midgame interview, the young forward beamed with confidence all while knowing that he has plenty of room to grow still.

"I'm always at 100%. Just trust the process. That's why I'm here. That's why I was on the court. I deserve it. I just played the right way. But I gotta be better defensively. I gotta be better. That's it," Salaun said, via Hornets Reddit on X.

Salaun did not add to his scoring tally in the second half, but the damage was already done. He provided a spark for the Hornets coming off the bench, and it's this kind of game that make his potential as a multi-dimensional two-way forward that tantalizing.

But finally, the important thing is that the Hornets offense finally showed signs of life, and against a good team like the Cavs as well. The goal now for Salaun and company is to build off of this performance, buying just enough time for both Miller and Knueppel to recover from their respective injuries.

Follow along while we bring you updates provided by teams — and the network — as players get medical attention, are ruled out, or hopefully return to play.

Should the Buffalo Bills have injuries that alter their lineup, it might be helpful to know who is available as the next man up. You can read about who is active and who is not suiting up today here .

_____________________________________________________________________________

CB Christian Benford – wrist – Questionable to Return Returned to Play

Benford has been trailing Justin Jefferson for 30 minutes. In the final two minutes of the half, Jefferson finally caught a couple of passes. On one of them, with the clock ticking, Benford ended up out of bounds and stayed on the ground a second too long for comfort. Reports were that he was carted to the locker room just ahead of halftime, and the Bills soon announced that the cornerback was questionable to return.

When the teams returned for the third quarter, Benford was on the field with his wrist heavily taped.

S Damar Hamlin – cramping – Probable to Return Returned to Play

When the Bills' defense took the field to start the third quarter, they were without one of the guys head coach Joe Brady said is key to the team's communication. Damar Hamlin stayed behind in the locker room to get IV treatment for cramps.

The Minnesota quarterback had his foot stepped on by one of his lineman near the end of the third quarter. The Vikings took a timeout to give him time to walk it off. It didn't help. Wentz was visibly struggling as he launched a third down pass that fell harmless to the ground and limped off the field as quickly as possible while the quarter expired. Wentz went to the medical tent as third string quarterback Max Brosmer began warming up. Kyler Murray was inactive tonight with a hamstring injury.

The Vikings were working against Josh Allen who was orchestrating a drive to get the Bills in field goal range. Ingram-Dawkins ended up down on the field and was unable to walk off the field unassisted.
