articles.title: Purdue Uses a 21-2 Run to Blow By Illinois State: 76-59
articles.summary: Purdue used a big run to put this one away.
articles.body:
Purdue came into this game looking to avoid their first 0-3 start since the 1950-1951 season. A season in which they finished 8-14 and 4-10 in conference play. Standing in their way was an Illinois State team from The Valley. Purdue changes up the starting lineup as you would expect with Antione West Jr. and Jack Benter being slotted in place of Omer Mayer and Gicarri Harris. The writing was on the wall with that one given the substitution pattern you saw in the two overtimes from the game against Valparaiso.

John Wooden Memorial Player of the Game (JWMPOTG): Giving this one to Antione West Jr. in what I hope is his coming out party. The redshirt freshman went 7-11 from the floor including 3-4 from three and helped spark the run that put this game out of reach.

Purdue needed to do a number of things to return a little bit of hope to the fanbase. First and foremost they needed to win. That's always number one. Second though, they needed to shoot the ball better, show better effort on defense, and maybe, just maybe, play a full 40 minutes.

If Buddy the Elf can recharge in just 40 minutes there's no reason that this Purdue men's basketball team can't play a good 40 minutes of basketball.

While Purdue looked better in the first half than they did the last 30 minutes we saw them play, the second half and double overtime against Valparaiso, they still had plenty of problems. Purdue's offense too often resulted in clumps of players around the perimeter just sort of standing there. That's no way to run an offense. Purdue was also incredibly streaky in the first half. At one point they hit seven shots in a row. Then, toward the end of the half they went 1-9. I won't say it was feast or famine because what we watched was no feast.

Purdue did shoot the three better in the first half but that might be partly because they shot far fewer. In the first half they went 4/10 from three. West hit two threes while Benter and Jacobsen added one a piece. Yes, Jacobsen. He was again Purdue's leading scorer heading into halftime as the only Boilermaker in double figures with 10. On defense the Boilermakers did a good job handling the Redbirds three point shooting. They came into this game shooting just over 50% from three in their first two games. In the first half of this one Purdue held them to 3-16 from three with one of those made threes being a bank in off the glass.

Despite these good numbers on defense Illinois State continued to chip away at the lead. Purdue never looked comfortable out there and went into half with a smaller lead than they had against Valparaiso on Friday. In that one Purdue went into halftime up 12 while here in Mackey Arena on Monday night Purdue headed to the locker room up just eight points at 36-28. Purdue got to 36 after West hit a nice three at the end of the first half.

The second half played out much like the second half against Valparaiso with Illinois State chipping away at the Purdue lead until it got down to two points at 50-48 with 8:55 to go. At that point I think everyone in the arena and everyone watching at home got that puckering feeling and some PTSD from Friday's game. If Purdue let this one slip away that 0-3 record would begin to weigh very heavy on this team. Then, Purdue ratcheted up the intensity on both ends of the floor. You might wonder who was on the court at that moment and I'll tell you. It was CJ Cox, Antione West Jr., Luke Ertel, Jack Benter, and Daniel Jacobsen. Purdue would go on a 26-11 run to end the game but a number of those Illinois State points came in garbage time. The real meat of the run happened from 8:55 to 2:33 when Purdue ballooned the lead from 50-48 to 71-50 at the 2:33 mark. That's a 21-2 run. Maybe Purdue unlocked something over that 6:22 span in the second half. Could those five be the starters for the next game of the season?

Some things that stand out in the box score here:

Omer Mayer played just 14 minutes. He was 1-3 from the floor.

Daniel Jacobsen led the Boilermakers with 20 points but took only 8 shots. I love the efficiency but the guy has to have more opportunities.

Could this be the Antione West Jr. coming out party? 7-11 from the floor and 3-4 from three.

Purdue was 8-19 from three for a much better 42%.

Purdue outrebounded the Redbirds 30-17. Those extra possessions made a huge difference when Purdue was struggling.

Look, it wasn't pretty, winning isn't always, but Purdue did what they needed to do and for six minutes in the second half Purdue looked like the team we all hoped they could be coming into this season. It's not going to be easy to replicate that intensity and that focus but it's what Purdue is going to have to do night in and night out if they want to compete this season. The margin for error is much smaller for this team than in year's past. Tonight was an good moment, but also a proof of concept of what this team can be.

articles.title: Bobby Durkin hits game-winner to beat Cincinnati 63-61
articles.summary: Bobby Durkin hits game-winner for the Gophers
articles.body:
After trailing for most of the second half, the Gophers scrambled to come back and Bobby Durkin hit a deep three in the final seconds to beat the Cincinnati Bearcats 63-61 and remain undefeated. Kyan Evans did most of the work throughout the game, scoring 26 points, grabbing 10 rebounds and five assists. But it was Isaac Asuma, advancing the ball to Bobby Durkin, who hit his only three of the game to give Minnesota the lead with 0.4 on the clock and essentially sealing the win for Minnesota.

Minnesota jumped out to an early lead and seemed to be controlling the game for the first 10 minutes of the game. But then Cincinnati just slowly took control of the pace of the game, playing good defense and making things difficult for everyone on the Gopher offense except Evans.

The Bearcats forced a ton of Gopher turnovers that they turned into points, but Minnesota battled back and Durkin put the nail in the coffin to push the Gophers to 3-0 on the young season.

WHY IT MATTERED: The win is great, being 3-0 is great, but this will count as a Quad 1 win for the Gophers and is the best non-conference win since beating North Carolina and West Virginia in back-to-back games in 2011. This is a game that will benefit the Gophers as they try to get back to the NCAA Tournament.

GAME BALL: Evans had a double-double and his first big night scoring as a Gopher. But how do you not give the game ball to Bobby Buckets?

THE STAT : For Cincinnati, it was turnovers; for the Gophers, it was offensive rebounds. Both were garnering extra possessions for their team and frustrating their fans. Cincy forced 17 turnovers that resulted in 16 points. Minnesota grabbed 13 offensive rebounds that allowed them to score 11 bonus points.

TURNING POINT : This one was definitely in favor of the Bearcats, with a 79% chance of winning with 17 seconds left. And then MJ Collins missed the front end of a 1-and-1 and Asuma found Durkin for the game-winner.

HOT : Cincinnati's Tylen Riley has scored 11 points this season, but he was on fire tonight. The senior guard was 8/17 and 6/9 from three to finish with 25 points.

NOT : Durkin had just two points and was 0-5 from three this game before he hit the game-winner. He had two threes blocked and looked out-of-sorts for most of this game.

UP NEXT: The Gophers get a couple of gimme-games with Southern and Western Illinois coming to the Barn before three straight games against Power 5 teams. Southern is on Thursday at 7:00.

articles.title: Notre Dame dominates Eastern Illinois for a 94-70 win at home
articles.summary: The Irish keep steamrolling along with their early schedule.
articles.body:
The Notre Dame Fighting Irish are now 3-0 to start college basketball season, and they are doing it in a fashion we haven't seen in a while — even against smaller school. Notre Dame beat Eastern Illinois, 94-70, and had 5 players with double digit points. The biggest stat, however, was the 17 steals the Irish got — which is 4th best in school history.

Irish Roll in Scoring Frenzy Over Eastern Illinois, 94-70

SOUTH BEND, Ind. – The Notre Dame men's basketball team recorded the longest scoring run in Glenn & Stacey Murphy Head Coach Micah Shrewsberry's tenure Monday night against Eastern Illinois, posting a 24-0 scoring spree over seven minutes in the first half. In addition, all five Fighting Irish (3-0) starters finished in double digits, led by a 20-point performance from Logan Duncomb. As a result, the Irish rolled to a 94-70 victory over the Panthers (0-3). Duncomb recorded a perfect 9-for-9 shooting night, plus added four boards and two assists. Fifth-year point guard Braeden Smith was once again all over the stat sheet. He posted 17 points on 6-of-8 shooting, dished out a team-best eight assists, grabbed five rebounds and collected a team-high five steals. Smith now has 21 assists through three games and is one assist shy of 500 in his career. Fifth-year guard Ethan Roberts earned 14 points on 5-of-9 shooting, which included three triples. He's now 7-of-12 from beyond the arc this season. Braeden Shrewsberry, like Roberts, has started the year with three straight games in double figures, finishing with 12 tonight. Shrewsberry dished out a career-high tying five assists, earned a career-high tying three steals and drained four triples. The senior has now moved into sole seventh place all-time on ND's career three-pointer list with 250. The Blue & Gold netted 17 steals against the Panthers, which ranks fourth all-time for a single game, and the most since Jan. 6, 2002. The Irish forced 23 turnovers tonight and this comes just two games after forcing 20 from Villanova. ND tallied 28 points off said turnovers. Offensively, Notre Dame shot 58.9 percent from the floor and 45.8 percent from beyond the arc. They also dished out a season-best 20 assists. HOW IT HAPPENED Eastern Illinois had recorded three triples through two games, so naturally the Panthers started the game Monday night 3-for-3 from beyond the arc to open up an 11-0 lead. Out of the Notre Dame timeout, the home squad responded with the biggest scoring run in Coach Shrewsberry's four-year tenure – 24-0. Shrewsberry kicked off the offensive flurry with a three, which was followed by a steal and transition layup from Smith, then a low post-spin move and score from Duncomb. Couple that with a pair of Notre Dame free throws and a steal and dunk from Logan Imes, and the Irish took their first lead of the night at 12-11. Seven different Irish players scored during the 24-0 run, led by a combined 11 points from Shrewsberry and Koehler. Defensively, the Irish forced seven turnovers and held EIU scoreless for seven minutes. Later, the Panthers recorded a stretch in which they converted 6-of-9 from the field to stay within 10 points. Yet, Braeden Smith instantly killed the momentum with an and-one. In fact, Smith recorded eight of the team's final 10 points of the half. The Irish led 46-33 at halftime. The Irish shot a hot 61.5 percent in the first half, going 16-of-26 from the floor, and 45.5 percent from behind the arc (5-for-11). The Irish defense forced 12 turnovers, which they converted into 20 points. Smith and Roberts were both in double figures at the midway point, combining for 21 points. Smith was 4-for-4 from the floor, while Roberts was 4-for-6. Duncomb tallied the first six points for the Blue & Gold in the second half, bringing his point total to double digits. During the 17-minute mark, Shrewsberry and Roberts each drained a triple. Later at 14:52, Shrewsberry recorded his fourth triple of the night, pushing the lead to 20. The Irish didn't let up as they went on an 8-0 run over 1:06, while Smith went on a solo 5-0 run to make it 69-44 with 13:53 remaining. The trio of Koehler, Duncomb, and Smith would go on to score the next 14 points for the Irish as they surged Notre Dame to a 27-point lead at 83-56 with 7:28 to go. While the Panthers would counter with a 6-0 run, it was broken up by a pair of free throws from Devin Brown. Shortly after, Yoro Diallo was on the board with his first bucket of the night with 4:56 remaining as his layup would make it 87-64. The Irish and Panthers finished the night going basket-for-basket as Imes would score seven straight points for Notre Dame to close out the 94-70 victory. UP NEXT It's a very short turnaround for the Notre Dame men's program, which will be right back at it inside Purell Pavilion on Wednesday night vs. South Carolina State. Tip is slated for 7 p.m. ET on ACCNX

articles.title: ‘He’s the perfect teammate’: Urban Meyer defends Jeremiah Smith behavior after Oregon loss
articles.summary: Jeremiah Smith has been at the center of plenty of conversation since Ohio State’s blowout loss to Oregon on Saturday, after the star wide receiver was caugh...
articles.body:
Jeremiah Smith has been at the center of plenty of conversation since Ohio State's blowout loss to Oregon on Saturday, after the star wide receiver was caught yelling toward the Buckeyes' sideline amidst the frustrating loss. Now, former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer has weighed in.

Speaking on The Triple Option podcast this week, Meyer said that he would "call him in" for a conversation about the moment, but Meyer he had nothing but praise for Smith, calling him "the perfect teammate" and urging him not to let anyone "question who you are."

Ohio State jumped out to a 14-0 lead against Oregon at Ohio Stadium, but the Ducks scored 38 straight points on their way to a 41-28 win. The loss was the Buckeyes' second straight and dropped them to 6-3 on the season.

Smith went more than two full quarters without a catch, and late in the third quarter, he was seen screaming toward the sideline after finally hauling in a pass. He finished the game with seven catches for 133 yards and a touchdown, but by then the game was well out of reach.

After the game, longtime Ohio State reporter Jeremy Birmingham, who covers the Buckeyes for 97.1 The Fan, ripped Smith for his outburst , saying that he can't go "stomping down the field like a petulant child." Smith later reposted a defense of himself from former Ohio State center LeCharles Bentley.

During this week's episode of The Triple Option , host Rob Stone brought up the criticism Smith has been receiving, saying that he read the moment as frustration with where Ohio State is right now. He then asked Meyer how he would have handled the situation.

Meyer said that he would have called him in for a conversation, but he made it clear that he has no concerns about Smith's character.

"I would probably call him in and sit down and talk to him, and I know Jeremiah, but I don't know him. I know him because of what Coach Day and the strength coach and everyone tells me about this kid. And he's the perfect teammate. He's the perfect worker. He's got a lifestyle that there's no question marks to it," Meyer said, on the podcast .

Meyer added that Smith simply needs to remember how much attention he draws, given his status as the most high-profile player on the team.

"So I'd call him and just say, realize the camera is on you as much as it is anyone else, probably anywhere else in the United States of America, and he's earned that. So just hustle back and, you know, don't let anybody start to question who you are," Meyer said.

Clearly, Meyer isn't worried about Smith. But with Ohio State's season on the line, all eyes will be on the star receiver over the final three weeks of the regular season.

articles.title: Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving combine for 78 points, erase 13-point Pacers lead in 125-122 Mavs' win
articles.summary: Pascal Siakam has monster first half but Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving were too much in a 125-122 Mavericks win over the Pacers
articles.body:
See the best photos from Pacers vs Mavericks

DALLAS -- Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving exploded for a combined 78 points to erase a 13-point Pacers lead and give the Mavericks a 125-122 win at the American Airlines Center on Monday night.

The Pacers fell to 3-8 with their second straight loss. The Mavericks improved to 7-4.

Flagg posted 43 points on 16 of 25 shooting, grabbed 10 rebounds and dished out six assists. Irving scored 35 points and hit on 7 of 10 3-pointers. Pascal Siakam led the Pacers with 29 points, 26 coming in the first half. Aaron Nesmith scored 18 points, cener Ivica Zubac had 16 points. Kelly Oubre Jr. had 14.

Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving go berserk on Pacers

The Pacers corrected a lot of their problems from Saturday's loss to the Nuggets. They had a much stronger first-half performance. They shared the ball, shot it reasonably well and fought on the defensive end. But they simply had no antidote for one of the most potent starting backcourts in the NBA on a night when both of its members were sizzling.

Irving and Flagg, both former No. 1 picks out of Duke, hit inferno levels against the Pacers and produced more than half of the Mavericks' total production. They combined for 78 points on 27 of 43 shooting including 10 of 16 from 3-point range.

Flagg, the 6-9 wing functioning as a shooting guard -- and a great one -- scored 43 points on 16 of 25 shooting, including 3 of 6 from 3-point range, and also hit 8 of 8 free throws. He added 10 rebounds and dished out six assists. Irving, the 15-year veteran and nine-time All-Star, had a vintage performance that showed little evidence of his ACL tear last year. He finished with 35 points on 11 of 18 shooting including a shimmering 7 of 10 from 3-point range.

The Pacers hung around long enough to have a chance in the final minute, but late buckets by Flagg put the game away. He answered three Aaron Nesmith foul shots with a critical jumper to put the Mavericks up four with 1:02 to play. Then after a Nesmith 3-pointer, he hit a jumper on offensive rebound by Naji Marshall off Marshall's own missed free throw to put the Mavs up three with 26 seconds left. Two key free throws by Irving helped the Mavericks put the game away.

Pascal Siakam brilliant in first half, swarmed in second

With Tyrese Haliburton still out, the Pacers have been in need of something next level from Siakam to carry the squad. He's been solid throughout the Pacers' tough start and entered Monday averaging 21.4 points per game on 51.7% shooting, but he hadn't scored 30 points since the season opening win over the Pelicans and had only surpassed 25 points twice all season. It was even more imperative because they were up against Irving and Flagg.

Siakam certainly gave the Pacers everything they could have asked for in the first half. He hit his first eight field goals and his first five 3-pointers before finally missing a heat-check 3 in the final minutes of the second quarter. At the break he had 26 points on 8 of 9 shooting, six rebounds, four assists, no turnovers and no fouls, posting a +15 plus-minus figure in just 16 minutes of game action. In the second half, however he was swarmed with constant double and triple teams and scored just three points on 1 of 7 shooting.

Kelly Oubre Jr. gives one of his best efforts

The Pacers have been waiting for a breakout game from off-season free-agent signing Kelly Oubre Jr. as he entered Monday's game averaging just 8.5 points and 2.4 rebounds per game, shooting 41% from the floor and just over 23% from 3-point range. There's still certainly another level the Pacers would still like to see, but Monday's performance was a step in the right direction on both ends.

The long-armed 6-8 wing scored 14 points on 6 of 9 shooting including 1 of 3 from 3-point range. He had two rebounds but also gave the Pacers a defensive option off the bench they could use on Irving, Flagg and others.

articles.title: Jacobsen scores 20 points and Purdue gets first win of the season, 76-59 over Illinois State
articles.summary: (AP) — Daniel Jacobsen scored 20 points and Purdue beat Illinois State 76-59 on Monday night for the Boilermakers first win of the season. Purdue (1-2) lost...
articles.body:
WEST LAFAYETTE, Ind. (AP) — Daniel Jacobsen scored 20 points and Purdue beat Illinois State 76-59 on Monday night for the Boilermakers first win of the season.

Purdue (1-2) lost its season opener to then-No. 15 Gonzaga, 78-72 in Las Vegas, and its home-opener 83-80 on a buzzer-beater in double overtime to Valparaiso.

The Boilermakers never trailed against Illinois State, shooting 56.5% (26 of 46) from the floor and 8 of 19 from long range. They entered shooting 10 of 49 from distance.

Antione West Jr. added 17 points for Purdue. Jack Benter scored 14 points and C.J. Cox chipped in with 10.

Johnny Kinziger and Noah Cleveland scored 12 points apiece for Illinois State (1-2). Malik Messina-Moore added 11 points and Demarion Burch had 10.

West's 3-pointer ended the first half and gave Purdue a 36-28 halftime lead. Jacobsen scored 10 first-half points for the Boilermakers.

Cleveland's two free throws cut the Cardinals' deficit to 50-48 with 8:55 remaining. Purdue answered with a 17-0 run to pull away.

Illinois State: at North Dakota State on Friday.

COLLEGE STATION, Texas (AP) — PJ Haagerty scored 22 points on 9-of-13 shooting and Texas A&M walloped Louisiana-Monroe 108-67 on Monday night.

Jordan Pope scored 19 points for Texas A&M (3-0), and reserves Tyshawn Archie and Zach Clemence scored 12 and 10 respectively.

In shooting 52% (38 of 73) overall, the Aggies saw 13 players enter the scoring column. Texas A&M built a 16-3 lead and never trailed. They were up 54-27 at halftime.

Quaran McPherson scored 16 points and reserve Khalil London 12 for Louisiana-Monroe (1-2).

On Friday night, Texas A&M trampled Northern Kentucky 104-67. Last year, Texas A&M topped the century mark a program record six times.

Texas A&M so far this season is averaging 103 points per game.

Louisiana-Monroe: heads to TCU to face the Horned Frogs on Wednesday.

Texas A&M: hosts Oklahoma State on Thursday.

articles.title: Iowa football to gift Northwestern game ball to Jack Campbell
articles.summary: After Iowa's win, Kirk Ferentz said the Hawkeyes would be gifting the Northwestern game ball to Jack Campbell.
articles.body:
Following No. 15 Iowa 's (7-2, 4-2 Big Ten) 24-10 road win over Northwestern (6-3, 3-3 Big Ten) at the new Ryan Field on Saturday, head coach Kirk Ferentz said former Hawkeyes and current Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell would be getting a game ball.

Campbell was carted off the field with a neck injury in the Lions ' Week 8 win over the Vikings after making a tackle against another former Hawkeye and current Minnesota tight end, T.J. Hockenson, on Nov. 1. The Hawkeye great has been on Iowa fans' hearts and minds since.

"All the feedback has been really positive," Ferentz said in his postgame media availability. "Hearing some encouraging news, it's going to be an – I don't know how long road – but it's moving in the right direction. Thought that was really fitting certainly to give him a ball and we'll get that to him."

Campbell has been hospitalized with his neck injury, but released a statement last week saying that he has "full movement" in his lower body and he's "continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body."

"I think all of you know just how impactful Jack was in our program, what a tremendous person he is, what a tremendous player he's been for us, and then now he's moved on and done the same exact thing in Detroit," Ferentz said last Tuesday. "Not only playing really well, but just a tremendous leader and tremendous addition. So we're all keeping him in our thoughts, and certainly, you know, hope everybody that's a Hawkeye fan does the same."

Like his Lions teammates , the Hawkeyes will look to honor Campbell's Iowa legacy as he continues to recover with their play down the stretch of the 2026 regular season. Iowa hosts Purdue (3-6, 2-4 Big Ten) on Saturday, Nov. 14. That matchup against the Boilermakers is set for a 6:30 p.m. kickoff on NBC and Peacock.

articles.title: Shorthanded Hornets nail 23 3-pointers, beat Cavaliers to end six-game skid
articles.summary: The Charlotte Hornets found their shooting rhythm Monday night, defeating the Cavaliers 124-112 to end a six-game losing streak.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets came out with plenty of energy Monday night, as the team hoped to snap a six-game losing streak against the Cleveland Cavaliers. Charlotte got off on the right foot, outscoring the Cavaliers 40-25 in the second quarter to take a 16-point lead into the halftime break. Grayson Allen had another stellar first half, scoring 20 points.

In the third quarter, Charlotte's lead ballooned to as many as 33, but Cleveland's third unit helped claw back in the fourth quarter. The Cavaliers outscored Charlotte 32-17 in the fourth, cutting the lead down to as many as eight. That said, the Hornets held on 124-112, as a pivotal offensive rebound by Ryan Kalkbrenner led to a Royce O'Neale 3-pointer to ice the game with 2:44 left to play.

In the absence of Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel, it was Naz Reid and Grayson Allen who provided the scoring. Allen finished with a game-high 27 points to go along with six assists, four rebounds and two steals. Reid tallied a double-double with 25 points, 13 rebounds, four assists and two steals. The aforementioned Kalkbrenner was phenomenal in place of Moussa Diabate (who was also injured). The former Creighton center posted eight points and 15 rebounds, 10 of which came on the offensive glass. He also had three blocks and one steal. Rookie Meleek Thomas was Cleveland's leading scorer, finishing with 18 points off the bench with three rebounds, three assists, two blocks and two steals.

Looking ahead, the Hornets will now embark on a four-game road trip beginning Thursday against the Phoenix Suns .

articles.title: Jets coach criticizes Devils’ decision not to play Connor Hellebuyck in Winnipeg
articles.summary: Winnipeg coach Scott Arniel criticized the Devils’ decision to sit Connor Hellebuyck against the Jets, saying it only prolongs an already difficult chapter b...
articles.body:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba — Winnipeg coach Scott Arniel said he's disappointed Connor Hellebuyck won't play against the Jets Tuesday night, arguing the decision made by the New Jersey Devils only prolongs a difficult chapter for the organization in the aftermath of granting the goaltender's public request to be traded.

"It's their decision, and they can do whatever they want," Arniel said Monday after practice. "I think that it would put closure to it. This doesn't."

The Devils said Sunday night that Hellebuyck would not play at Winnipeg, citing analysis that it would reduce their probability of winning. Hellebuyck has won all five of his starts with New Jersey.

"I've seen a lot of analytics in my life since it's really come into the forefront," Arniel said. "I'm not sure how this works into the analytics part of it."

Hellebuyck spent 11 seasons with the Jets, winning the Vezina Trophy as the NHL's top goalie three times and the Hart Trophy as MVP in 2024-25. During the offseason, he asked for a trade that finally happened on Oct. 23 after he refused to report for training camp and was suspended without pay well into the season.

"I mean, he just gave up on us," Arniel said. "And so it'll be nice to just finally be done with this."

The Jets visit the Devils on Nov. 28 in the second and final meeting between the teams this season. Arniel expects more questions about Hellebuyck leading up to that game.

Jets captain Adam Lowry acknowledged he was surprised by the decision.

"Oh, I would have loved to play against him," Lowry said. "We'd all be lying if we said we weren't looking forward to the opportunity."

After posting a shutout at Toronto, Hellebuyck said he wanted to play against his former team but understands the Devils' decision. The 33-year-old American added that he plans to explain his reasons for wanting out when he speaks to reporters in Winnipeg on Tuesday.

articles.title: Rockets Player Ratings: Durant Posts Near Triple-Double In Win Over Nuggets
articles.summary: The Houston Rockets snapped their two-game losing streak behind a near triple-double from Kevin Durant against the Denver Nuggets.
articles.body:
The Houston Rockets picked up an impressive victory over the Denver Nuggets , winning 110-100 behind a balanced offensive attack, dominant rebounding, and a strong bounce-back performance from Kevin Durant . The veteran superstar flirted with a triple-double, finishing with 23 points, 12 rebounds, and eight assists while navigating a challenging shooting night.

Houston's supporting cast made the difference. Alperen Sengun delivered an efficient 20-point performance with 11 rebounds and eight assists, while Jabari Smith Jr. contributed 14 points and seven rebounds. The Rockets also dominated the glass, collecting 50 rebounds compared to Denver's 39, and generated 29 assists to keep their offense moving.

Tari Eason provided a massive spark off the bench with 12 points, five rebounds, two steals, and a game-high +18 rating. Houston built a lead as large as 19 points and controlled the game for most of the night.

Here are the Rockets' player ratings from the win.

Game Stats: 23 PTS, 12 REB, 8 AST, 1 BLK, 6 TOV, 6-15 FG, 1-3 3-PT FG, 10-10 FT, 36 MIN

Durant came within two assists of a triple-double, and his ability to contribute across multiple categories was crucial to Houston's victory. His 12 rebounds and eight assists highlighted how much responsibility he carried beyond scoring.

The shooting efficiency wasn't quite there, and six turnovers are certainly worth mentioning. Still, Durant made up for those shortcomings by getting to the free-throw line consistently and delivering a productive all-around performance.

Game Stats: 20 PTS, 11 REB, 8 AST, 1 STL, 1 BLK, 2 TOV, 9-17 FG, 1-3 3-PT FG, 1-3 FT, 35 MIN

Sengun was one of Houston's most important players, nearly recording a triple-double of his own. His combination of scoring, rebounding, and playmaking gave the Rockets a significant advantage offensively.

Eight assists from the center position are particularly impressive, and his 20 points came on an efficient 9-17 shooting. The missed free throws prevent this from being an even cleaner performance, but Sengun was excellent overall.

Game Stats: 14 PTS, 7 REB, 3 AST, 6-13 FG, 2-8 3-PT FG, 38 MIN

Smith provided valuable scoring and rebounding while taking care of the basketball. His two three-pointers helped stretch Denver's defense, although the eight attempts from beyond the arc came with inconsistent results.

The biggest positive was his clean decision-making. Three assists and zero turnovers in 38 minutes gave Houston another dependable contributor.

Game Stats: 12 PTS, 5 REB, 2 AST, 2 STL, 1 BLK, 5-11 FG, 2-6 3-PT FG, 19 MIN

Eason was arguably Houston's most impactful bench player. He scored 12 points in just 19 minutes, added five rebounds, and contributed two steals and a block without committing a turnover.

His +18 was the best mark on the Rockets, reflecting the energy and defensive intensity he brought to the floor. Eason gave Houston exactly the kind of spark that can swing a game.

Game Stats: 12 PTS, 1 REB, 2 AST, 1 TOV, 4-9 FG, 3-6 3-PT FG, 1-2 FT, 30 MIN

VanVleet knocked down three triples and provided some much-needed perimeter scoring. He wasn't asked to carry the offense, but he made his minutes count by shooting efficiently from outside.

His playmaking numbers were relatively modest, although Houston's overall offensive movement made up for that. A solid, complementary performance.

Game Stats: 8 PTS, 9 REB, 3 AST, 1 STL, 1 TOV, 3-8 FG, 2-2 FT, 35 MIN

Thompson didn't have a particularly productive scoring night, but his impact was felt in other areas. Nine rebounds, three assists, and a steal demonstrated his versatility and willingness to do the dirty work.

His athleticism and defensive activity remain important ingredients in Houston's identity. The scoring could have been better, but Thompson contributed to a winning effort.

Game Stats: 5 PTS, 2 REB, 2 AST, 1 STL, 2-5 FG, 1-3 3-PT FG, 17 MIN

Smart played a useful supporting role, contributing defensively while keeping his offensive game simple. Five points weren't particularly eye-catching, but he added two assists and a steal without turning the ball over.

His experience and defensive instincts remain valuable in a game where Houston needed to maintain its intensity.

Game Stats: 8 PTS, 3 REB, 1 AST, 3-5 FG, 2-2 3-PT FG, 12 MIN

Bogdanovic delivered an efficient offensive contribution off the bench. He knocked down both of his three-point attempts and finished with eight points in only 12 minutes.

Houston needed additional perimeter shooting, and Bogdanovic provided it without forcing anything.

Game Stats: 8 PTS, 3-8 FG, 2-7 3-PT FG, 17 MIN

Sheppard contributed eight points and two three-pointers, although his shooting was somewhat inconsistent. He didn't contribute much outside scoring, but his ability to knock down perimeter shots helped Houston maintain offensive spacing.

articles.title: Durant and Sengun power the Rockets past the Nuggets 110-100 to snap a 2-game skid
articles.summary: HOUSTON (AP) — Kevin Durant had 23 points and Alperen Sengun added 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 110-100 win over the Denver Nuggets on Monday night th...
articles.body:
HOUSTON (AP) — Kevin Durant had 23 points and Alperen Sengun added 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 110-100 win over the Denver Nuggets on Monday night that snapped a two-game skid.

Denver's Jamal Murray made two free throws to cut the lead to six points with about five minutes left. But Christian Braun missed a pair of free throws after that and Houston got baskets from Sengun and Amen Thompson to push the lead to 100-90 with four minutes remaining.

The Rockets got back on track after losing to Minnesota and Phoenix following a 7-1 start to the season.

Murray had 38 points in his fourth game this season with at least 34 points as Denver's two-game winning streak ended. Nikola Jokic added 25 points and had 16 rebounds and eight assists.

Four quick points by Murray, with the help of a turnover by Sengun, got the Nuggets within four points with less than seven minutes to go.

But a short basket by Sengun followed by a 3-pointer from Fred VanVleet extended Houston's lead to 96-87 with 5 1/2 minutes remaining.

The Rockets had a 16-point lead early in the third quarter before the Nuggets used an 18-2 run to tie it at 60-60 with about five minutes left in the quarter.

Jokic, Murray and Cameron Johnson all made 3-pointers to power that run while the Rockets missed nine consecutive shots and had two turnovers. Their only points in that stretch came on a pair of free throws by Durant.

Houston got its first field goal in more than 6 1/2 minutes on a basket by Tari Eason with about four minutes left in the third. That was the start of an 11-2 run that made it 71-62.

Denver visits the Grizzlies on Wednesday night.

The Rockets host Golden State Wednesday night.

articles.title: In cross country, a home run could produce a grand slam
articles.summary: Cross-country courses are like snowflakes, and sometimes in late autumn are just as wet — though neither snowflakes nor raindrops are forecast for Friday, wh...
articles.body:
Cross-country courses are like snowflakes, and sometimes in late autumn are just as wet — though neither snowflakes nor raindrops are forecast for Friday, when the New Mexico Lobos will pursue twin trophies at the NCAA Mountain Regional on the UNM North Golf Course.

And beyond the obvious advantages for the home team — Albuquerque's 5,000-foot elevation, no planes or trains involved, encouragement from fans — the course itself offers some benefits.

First and foremost, there's familiarity. On Sept. 15, the Lobos opened their 2026 season with their own invitational meet at the North Course. That's been an annual event.

"Yeah, it's a big advantage," UNM track/cross-country coach Darren Gauson said at Monday's weekly news conference. "Not all (his athletes) have competed there, but they're pretty familiar with it. So, yeah, you take everything you can.

"The course, being at home, getting some friends and family out there supporting the team. That all goes into our advantage."

But there's more. The course at the North Course — the North Course course, if you prefer — is tighter than most; three laps with several twists and turns. It's spectator-friendly, and coach-friendly, too.

"Yeah, the smaller the course the better," Gauson said. "Sometimes you just get to see (the runners) a little bit more, give them some feedback and just know where we are in the race.

"That's going to be important, especially for regionals."

Entering Friday's races, the UNM men are ranked No. 1 in the nation but with Colorado, a Mountain Regional rival, a close second. The Lobo women are sixth, behind two teams that will run at the North Course on Friday: No. 1 BYU and No. 5 Northern Arizona.

With nationals looming on Nov. 21 in Terre Haute, Indiana, Gauson needs to finesse his lineups to win regionals while making sure his top athletes are healthy and rested for Terre Haute.

"You don't want to get into a fistfight at regionals," Gauson said, referring in particular to Colorado in the men's race. And then (if you do), both teams are a little toasted going into nationals. So we've got to be careful, not just go all out against the number two team."

The Lobos had the top seven men's finishers at the recent Mountain West Conference championship — UNM won with a perfect team score of 15 — so any lineup Gauson selects will be more than formidable.

Gauson will be selective with his women's lineup as well but said Marion Jepngetich, the 2026 NCAA 5,000-meters champion on the track, will run her first cross-country meet of the season on Friday.

SOCCER: When Karley Nelson was promoted from assistant coach to head coach at UNM almost exactly one year ago, replacing her former boss Heather Dyche, the returning players were ecstatic.

Yet, when an assistant coach is promoted to head coach, the player-coach relationship changes. It's inevitable.

But Nelson, looking back at her just-completed first season in charge, believes the transition has been a smooth one.

The record supports her. Though the Lobos barely missed qualifying for the Mountain West Conference tournament, they finished with a record of 8-4-5, 5-2-3 in conference play.

Would Nelson have done anything differently? Of course, since there were team goals not met.

Even so, Nelson said that the necessary adjustments were made in the coaching transition — and were not drastic ones in any case.

"The players have always joked, even when I was an assistant here, that I was the serious one of the three (coaches)," she said. "I think the players knew that when we're out in the field, it's business.

"My tone as a head coach has had to change a little bit because at the end of the day, I have the final say. … But I think that the way I interact with the players, or the way I run a session or the demands of the players, my expectations of the players, that hasn't changed much. I think that stayed pretty consistent throughout."

VOLLEYBALL: Not that long ago, the Lobos were 7-3 in Mountain West play and seemed well on their way to a top-four finish and a berth in the conference tournament in coach Brian Hosfeld's first season.

Now, as they prepare for Thursday-Saturday matches at UNLV, they're 7-7 (9-15 overall) with their tournament chances flickering.

League leader Hawaii (13-1) has clinched a tournament berth with four matches remaining. They're followed by Grand Canyon and UC Davis, both at 9-5, and UTEP at 8-6.

New Mexico and UNLV are tied for fifth place at 7-7, and common sense tells the Lobos that if they're to make the tournament they must achieve no worse than a split in Vegas. Only two more matches will remain: at home vs. Wyoming (6-8), to be played Nov. 18-19.

articles.title: Flagg has 43 points, 10 rebounds, Irving 35 points in Mavericks' 125-122 win over Pacers
articles.summary: DALLAS (AP) — Cooper Flagg had 43 points and 10 rebounds and Kyrie Irving scored 35 while completing a back-to-back for the first time this season as the Dal...
articles.body:
DALLAS (AP) — Cooper Flagg had 43 points and 10 rebounds and Kyrie Irving scored 35 while completing a back-to-back for the first time this season as the Dallas Mavericks rallied past the Indiana Pacers 125-122 on Monday night.

P.J. Washington Jr. could have extened the Dallas lead with four seconds left but missed both free throws, with Indiana's Obi Toppin grabbing the rebound. The Pacers' final possession ended with Dallas' Caleb Martin tipping away a pass by Andrew Nembhard near the sideline.

Flagg had a season-high in scoring while Irving tied for his season best. They combined to score 26 points in the fourth quarter — including Dallas' first 13 — as the Mavericks outscored the Pacers 35-29.

Irving, in action this season after missing 19 months with a torn ACL, played 28 minutes in Sunday night's 130-93 rout of Brooklyn and a season-high 38 minutes against Indiana after sitting out the second game of the Mavericks' first back-to-back 2½ weeks ago. He hit a season-high seven 3-pointers.

Dallas (7-4) swept a three-game homestand and is three games over .500 for the first time since March 1, 2025 (at 32-29).

Flagg has four straight double-doubles and five this season.

The Pacers (3-8) were led by Pascal Siakam with 29 points, but only three of those were scored in the second half. Aaron Nesmith scored 18 points with two of his four 3-pointers coming in the final minute.

Siakam hit 8 of 9 from the floor during the first half, including 5 of 6 behind the arc, plus 5 of 6 from the line for 26 points. He was the lone Pacer in double figures in building a 13-point lead that was 66-56 at halftime.

articles.title: Auburn basketball's Tahaad Pettiford stays hot against App State: 3 takeaways
articles.summary: Auburn basketball breezed past Appalachian State for a second consecutive victory Monday. Here's three takeaways.
articles.body:
AUBURN — In 80 minutes of game time, Auburn basketball has looked on cruise control, going from a 33-point win against Southeastern Louisiana to open the season and following it up with a 75-53 win against Appalachian State on Monday, Nov. 9, at Neville Arena.

It was nearly wire-to-wire dominance for Auburn (2-0), as the Tigers scored 10 unanswered points after Appalachian State (2-1) sunk a 3-pointer for the first basket of the contest. Auburn's largest lead of the night, 22 points, was reflected in the final score.

Here's three takeaways from Auburn's latest contest, with a look at individual standouts and more.

Tahaad Pettiford goes from strong finish to fast start against App State

After an 0-for-8 start against Southeastern, Pettiford finished as the game's leading scorer. He again had the night's leading point total Monday, with 26, but that began with him scoring Auburn's first 8 points.

Pettiford was efficient, too, making 50% of his shots from the floor and going 3 for 5 from 3-point range.

Narcisse Ngoy shows he's making headway with Auburn basketball

The box score didn't quite show it, but Auburn's 7-foot Frenchman continued to settle in against Appalachian State, and the best example may have been the scraps. Twice in the first half, Ngoy got tangled with a Mountaineer defender, hearing "Nar-cisse" chants from The Jungle student section the second time around.

In that instance, Ngoy was called for a technical foul upon review, but his 6-point scoring total was far from underwhelming. He did so on 3-for-5 shooting, and he posted 11 rebounds and a block in 14 minutes.

Auburn basketball delivers defensive buckle-down against App State

Appalachian State shot 44.4% from the field and 35.3% from beyond the arc in the first half, which included a barrage of 3-pointers to make it a one-possession contest at halftime.

Auburn's defense buckled down in the final 20 minutes however, as the Mountaineers shot 20.7% from the floor in the second half, making just one of 11 attempts from 3-point range.
